# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

## Problem

The 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 is
enforced only by review. Evidence of the gap: WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO decomposed
`database.ts` from 2,584 lines and closed as shipped, yet
`packages/shared/src/database.ts` is now 3,684 lines — the decomposition never

WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ, ...), each of which can regrow the same way.

## Goal

A cheap, deterministic check (script or test) that fails when a source file
exceeds 1,000 lines, with an explicit, shrinking allow-list for grandfathered
files so the check is green from day one and cannot silently regrow.

1. A check exists (script `scripts/check-file-size.ts` or a vitest unit test)
   that reports every non-test source file > 1,000 lines.
2. Grandfathered files are listed explicitly with their current line count, and
   the check fails if a listed file grows beyond its recorded budget.
3. The check is wired into an existing automated gate (pre-push or CI) without
   adding more than ~2 s to that gate.
4. Retiring an entry is required when an item from the WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7
   sweep completes a decomposition.

   passes.

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".
data.title: vitest.config.ts: remove dead top-level singleFork key (vitest 4 ignores it)

## Summary

Discovered during a `/skill:machine-hygiene` session (approval-gate output).
`scripts/evaluate.py` renders the Proposed actions table more than once in the
same run, and the three `renice` actions (node, pi, npm-exec-tsx) are each
proposed as separate numbered actions (observed as 2-4 duplicated by 5-7).

Impact: the operator sees 8 actions where there are 5 distinct remediations,
polluting the approval gate. The duplicate rows are also indistinguishable, so
approving "1" while declining "5" leaves the same target both executed and
skipped.

Fix: dedupe keep-first on `(action, target pids | scope)` and render the gate
findings exactly once per run.

Source: `discovered-from:machine-hygiene-session-2025-10-21`.

## Verified root cause (plan session)

Reproduced against `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/` in the SorraAgents repo
(the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` is byte-identical).

**A. Duplicate actions — `pressure_analysis.py`.**

- `analyze_pressures()` computes the top-3 RSS contributors **once**, then
  assigns the *same list object* to every elevated pressure
  (`pressure["contributors"] = contributors`).
- `propose_remediations()` loops pressures x contributors, emitting one
  `renice` per (pressure, contributor) for `memory_usage`, `memory_pressure`
  and `swap_usage`. Two elevated memory metrics x three contributors yields six
  `renice` actions for three distinct targets.
- `rank_actions()` only sorts by impact/risk ratio; it never dedupes, and
  `evaluate.py` never calls it.

Deterministic repro (synthetic metrics: `memory_usage` critical, `swap_usage`
warning, 3 RSS contributors): 6 actions, 3 distinct `(action, target)` pairs;
rows 1-3 are field-for-field identical to rows 4-6.

**B. Repeated rendering — `evaluate.py` / `tables.py`.**

- `render_approval_gate()` renders the Proposed actions table (copy 1).
- `prompt_for_approval()` renders it **again** before the prompt (copy 2).
- `render_human()` renders it a **third** time, together with a second copy of
  the before table and of the pressure analysis.

Measured on the interactive path: `## Proposed actions` appears 3 times and
`## Before` appears 2 times. On the `--yes` path the gate is skipped, so each
appears once. The work item's "twice" is therefore an undercount of the
interactive path, which is the observed run.

## Scope

In scope: dedupe proposals keep-first; render gate findings once per run.

Out of scope (recorded in Observations, not fixed here): `renice` safety checks
(current nice value, live test suites), ranking being unused by `evaluate.py`,
`--json` + interactive gating mixing prose and JSON, `TOP_CONTRIBUTORS` not
being configurable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `propose_remediations()` emits no two actions sharing a dedupe key
   of `(action, frozenset(target pids), target scope)`. A fixture with two
   elevated memory metrics (`memory_usage` + `swap_usage`) and three RSS
   contributors yields exactly 3 `renice` actions, not 6.
- **AC2** — Dedupe is keep-first: the surviving action is field-for-field
   identical to the first emitted duplicate (`action`, `target`, `reason`,
   `expected_impact`, `impact`, `risk`), so the relative order of distinct
   actions is unchanged.
- **AC3** — `rank_actions()` dedupes as well, so
   `rank_actions(propose_remediations(...))` and any caller passing a list that
   contains duplicates both return no duplicates ("dedupe before ranking").
- **AC4** — An interactive run prints the `## Proposed actions` table exactly
   once and the `## Before` table exactly once across the entire run (gate
   output plus final report), asserted with injected `input_fn`/`output_fn` and
   no real TTY.
- **AC5** — The `--yes` (auto-approve) path still prints both tables exactly
   once, and `--dry-run` and `--json` output shapes are unchanged.
- **AC6** — Approval stays row-accurate: approving row `n` of the displayed
   table approves that row, and `approved_count + declined_count` equals the
   number of displayed rows (no duplicate counted twice).

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py` — add `dedupe_actions()`
  and apply it in `propose_remediations()` and `rank_actions()`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/tables.py` — `prompt_for_approval()` gains
  `show_actions: bool = True` so a caller that already rendered the table can
  suppress the repeat; `render_approval_gate()` unchanged.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/evaluate.py` — record in the workflow result
  whether findings were already rendered; `render_human()` skips
  already-rendered findings; pass `show_actions=False` to the gate prompt.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` — dedupe unit tests.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_approval_gate.py` — single-render and
  row-accuracy tests.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_integration.py` — end-to-end section-count
  assertions for the interactive and `--yes` paths.

All paths are relative to the **SorraAgents** checkout
(`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`, branch `dev`). The installed copy under
`~/.pi/agent/skills/` is a build artefact refreshed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`
and must not be edited directly.

## Minimal implementation (test-first)

1. Add the failing tests first: duplicate-`renice` fixture (AC1/AC2),
   `rank_actions` dedupe (AC3), section counts for both paths (AC4/AC5),
   row accuracy (AC6).
2. `pressure_analysis.py`: `dedupe_actions(actions)` keyed on
   `(action, frozenset(pids | []), target.get("scope"))`, keeping the first
   occurrence; call it at the end of `propose_remediations()` and at the start
   of `rank_actions()`.
3. `tables.py`: add the `show_actions` parameter to `prompt_for_approval()`
   (default `True` preserves current behaviour and keeps existing tests green).
4. `evaluate.py`: add `findings_rendered` to the `run_workflow()` result (`True`
   when the gate printed findings); `render_human()` gains
   `include_findings: bool | None = None` defaulting to
   `not result.get("findings_rendered", False)`; pass `show_actions=False` in
   the gate's prompt call.
5. Docs: no `SKILL.md` change needed (internal behaviour); the skill tests are
   the contract.
6. Run the changed-scope test gate for the skill tests, then the dev-push full
   suite gate.

## Observations (not in scope — recorded, not fixed here)

- `renice` is proposed without inspecting the target's current nice value; the
  observed run targeted two live test suites already at nice 19/0. Tracked
  separately as a discovered item (see Appendix Q2).
- `evaluate.py` never calls `rank_actions()`, so actions are displayed in
  emission order rather than impact/risk order.
- `--json` without `--yes` still runs the interactive gate, mixing prose and
  JSON on stdout.
- `TOP_CONTRIBUTORS` is a module constant rather than a `config.yaml` tunable.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 (plan): effort/risk pre-check returned `skip` (Extra Small / Low).
  Ran the six automated review stages against the existing content; rewrote the
  description with a verified root cause, six testable ACs, `Key Files` and a
  test-first implementation sketch. No children created (single vertical
  slice); AC coverage review returned `proceed`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where does the fix land: the installed skill at
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` or the SorraAgents repo?**
  Answer (plan, evidence-based): the SorraAgents repo,
  `skill/machine-hygiene/`, on branch `dev`. Evidence: `diff` shows all three
  scripts byte-identical between repo and installed copy, and prior
  machine-hygiene work shipped from `skill/machine-hygiene/`
  (`WL-0MULOZ46M003THM1`, `WL-0MULP55W1009G62B`). Source: repo inspection,
  this session.
- **Q2 — Is the producer's secondary finding (renice without a nice-value
  check, targeting live test suites) part of this item?**
  Answer (plan assumption, pending producer confirmation): **no** — dedupe and
  single-render are the stated fix; the safety check is a separate behavioural
  change tracked as its own discovered item. **Recommended:** keep it separate
  — the dedupe fix is independently correct and testable, and merging widens an
  Extra Small chore into a semantics change requiring process-nice inspection.
  Evidence: the producer comment on this item labels it "Secondary finding",
  while the Summary/Fix line covers duplication only. Source: `@producer`
  comment 2026-10-21, this session's repro.
  **OPEN QUESTION** for `@producer`: if the nice-value guard must ship here
  instead, reply and the two items will be merged. Not blocking — the duplication
  fix stands on its own.

# Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled test, standup, refactor sessions at high priority

## Headline

A new ContextHub skill (`/skill:maintenance-routines`) that creates and maintains the required daily scheduled maintenance sessions (test 07:00, standup 08:00, refactor 09:00) in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatching all of them at **high request priority** so they are processed even in peak periods — backed by a herdr enhancement that threads a per-entry `priority` (default `high`) into the `X-Priority` request header.

## Problem statement

Every project should run regular automated maintenance routines (test suite, standup report, refactor pass). The herdr plugin already has the mechanism (`scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatched on idle by the downtime worker), but there is no maintained, canonical set: the current template/live config only carries `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (06:05, no priority), and **no** `/skill:test` routine. Worse, dispatched scheduled prompts have no work item, so they receive the downtime request-priority default `medium` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium`) — they can be starved behind peak-period contention. The operator wants the three routines scheduled daily (07:00/08:00/09:00) and dispatched at **high** priority.

## Users

- **Project operator** — wants the three routines to reliably exist in each project's schedule and to be processed even in peak periods.
- **Automated maintenance sessions** (`/skill:test`, `/skill:standup`, `/skill:refactor`) — must carry `X-Priority: high` on every provider request so `llama-proxy` serves them ahead of the contention queue.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I run `/skill:maintenance-routines` on a project and it ensures `/skill:test` (daily 07:00), `/skill:standup` (daily 08:00) and `/skill:refactor` (daily 09:00) are present and correctly configured in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, without touching my last-run timestamps or any custom entries.
- As an operator, I know every scheduled maintenance session is dispatched with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=high` (→ `X-Priority: high`), so the daily test/standup/refactor runs are served even during peak periods.
- As an operator, when I provision a new project with `wl init`, it comes pre-loaded with the same three routines (daily, timed, high priority).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Skill exists and reconciles the schedule.** `skill/maintenance-routines/` ships a `SKILL.md`, a reconciler script and unit tests. Invoking it (or the script directly) reconciles the project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (under the resolved worklog dir) so these required routines are present and exact:
   - `/skill:test` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "07:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:standup` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "08:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:refactor` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "09:00"`, `priority: "high"`
2. **Reconcile is non-destructive and idempotent.** Entries are created if absent; drifted fields (interval/time/priority) are corrected; `lastTriggeredAt` and all other user-defined entries are preserved verbatim; a second run makes no further changes; missing or malformed config files are handled fail-closed with a clear report; `--dry-run` shows the planned diff without writing.
3. **Herdr honours a per-entry `priority` field.** `ScheduledPrompt` gains an optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`) validated in `parseScheduledPrompt` (invalid value → entry skipped with a warning, fail-closed); **absent → defaults to `high`** for scheduled prompts. The scheduled-prompt dispatch passes it through `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (so `high` → `X-Priority: high` on every request). Unit tests cover parse defaults/validation and the dispatch threading.
4. **Template provisions the required set.** `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set) is updated to the three required routines with daily `intervalDays`, `time` and `priority: high`, so new projects are provisioned with the routines (create-if-absent semantics unchanged — existing configs are never clobbered).
5. **Documentation criterion.** `packages/herdr/README.md` (Scheduled prompts section), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (Request priority section) and `CONFIG.md` (Scheduled-prompts config section) document the new `priority` field, the default-`high` behaviour, and the three routines; the maintenance-routines skill is referenced from the relevant skill docs listing.
6. **Testing criterion.** Skill tests (`pytest` under `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/`) cover reconcile/idempotence/preservation/dry-run; herdr unit tests (`vitest`) cover the new parse/validation and dispatch priority; full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No changes to the interactive dispatch path or to the other downtime tiers' mapping tables** (`request-priority.ts` stays fixed); only the scheduled-prompt entry schema, its dispatch call, and the skill/template change.
- The requested **default is `high`** for scheduled prompts (operator decision Q1): an entry that wants lower priority must set the field explicitly (`low`/`medium`). This is a deliberate change from the current downtime default (`medium`) for scheduled prompts only.
- No code-behaviour changes to `wl init` — only the **contents** of `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the provisioning path and create-if-absent semantics stay as-is).
- The skill must be safe to run from any project root (`wl`-independent — it reads/writes only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, atomic tmp+rename, matching herdr's `saveScheduledPrompts` pattern).

## Existing state

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (and the live `/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`) currently carry only `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (daily `time: "06:05"`); no `/skill:test`; no priority field anywhere.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — schema (`id|prompt|intervalDays|lastTriggeredAt|time?`), fail-closed parse, due-check, atomic persist; **no priority support**.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` calls `spawnAgentPane(prompt.prompt, { model, cwd, paneName, anchorId })` with **no priority** → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions({ priority: undefined })` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium` (docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md, "Scheduled prompts have no work item and get the downtime default (medium)").
- `src/commands/init.ts` — `ensureScheduledPromptsInstalled` copies the template create-if-absent; unchanged in behaviour.
- Skills precedent: `skill/heartbeat/` and `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, tracked in ContextHub, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills/<name>`); shared helpers in `skill/shared/`.

## Desired change

1. **New skill** `skill/maintenance-routines/`: `SKILL.md` (spec: required-routines table, invocation, admission of a bootstrap `/skill:maintenance-routines` schedule), `scripts/maintenance_routines.py` (reconcile + `--dry-run`; atomic writes; preserves `lastTriggeredAt` and foreign entries), `tests/` (unit tests).
2. **Herdr priority support**: extend `ScheduledPrompt` + `parseScheduledPrompt` with optional `priority` (default `high`); thread it from `dispatchScheduledPrompt` → `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`. `mapDowntimeRequestPriority` already maps `high`→`high`.
3. **Template**: update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to the three routines (daily, timed, `priority: "high"`).
4. **Docs**: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md`; skill listed alongside heartbeat/pane-triage where appropriate.
5. **Tests**: pytest for the skill reconciler; vitest for parse/validation + dispatch threading in herdr.

## Key Files

- `skill/maintenance-routines/SKILL.md` — new skill spec (required-routines table, usage, dry-run).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py` — new reconciler CLI (`--dry-run`, atomic write, preserves state).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/test_maintenance_routines.py` — new unit tests (reconcile, idempotence, preservation, malformed config, dry-run).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`, default `high`), validation in `parseScheduledPrompt`.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` — new parse/default/validation cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` passes `prompt.priority` to `spawnAgentPane`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (or the scheduled-prompts tier test) — dispatch threads `priority: 'high'` into the spawn opts/env.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — updated to the three required routines.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the new field/default and the routines.
- `tests/skill/maintenance-routines/` — integration-style tests for the skill (repo test-suite convention, cf. `tests/skill/heartbeat/`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** (completed) — herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency) config — the mechanism the skill maintains.
- **WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH / WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed) — request priority (`X-Priority`) mapping tables and `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` env threading — the priority plumbing we reuse.
- **WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9** (completed) — removal of scheduled-prompts console output (no-op here).
- **WL-0MUKYERLZ006ELL5** (completed) — non-terminal cooldown for dispatched panes (context for scheduled dispatch behaviour).
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** (completed) — periodic request scheduling to the pi worklog plugin; the scheduled-prompts feature parent.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** – Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin (completed)
- **WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR** – Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier (completed)
- **WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6** – wl doctor (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, daily (+26 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: create, creates, daily, default, dispatched (+25 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, default (+23 more)
- Skill-authoring precedents: `skill/heartbeat/`, `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — default-`high` changes politeness of ALL scheduled prompts** (including custom future entries). Accepted by operator (Q1: "default high"); any entry can opt down via an explicit `low`/`medium` field. Mitigation: document prominently.
- **Risk — parse strictness.** An invalid `priority` value rejects the whole entry (consistent with existing `time` handling) — a config typo could silently disable a routine. Mitigation: the skill always writes a valid value; tests cover the failure path.
- **Risk — skill/template drift.** If `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` is later edited, the skill's required table may diverge. Mitigation: keep the required-routines table in one place (the skill), and the template mirrors it (as Q3).
- **Assumption — the skill runs per project root.** Invoked via a pi session (herdr pane or manual) with `cwd` at the project root; it reads/writes only `<cwd>/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (worklog-dir safe).
- **Assumption — operators may bootstrap the skill itself as a scheduled prompt** (e.g. daily `/skill:maintenance-routines`) to keep the schedule self-healing; not required for this item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to interactive dispatch, `request-priority.ts` tables, other downtime tiers, or `wl init` code; any opportunity discovered during implementation is recorded as a new linked work item, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: How should scheduled routines get high priority?**
  - Options: (a) per-entry `priority` field in `scheduled-prompts.json`, threaded through herdr dispatch → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`; (b) herdr always dispatches all scheduled prompts at `high`; (c) config-level default priority.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "1. A (default high)"** — per-entry field; **absent → default `high`**.
  - Reasoning recorded: matches "all those work items should be sent high priority so they get processed even in peak periods"; keeps intent in the config; future entries can opt down explicitly.
- **Q2: How strictly should the skill maintain the required set?**
  - Options: (a) ensure the three required routines exist & match spec (create-if-absent, fix drifted fields), keep other user entries; (b) strict whitelist (remove anything else); (c) create-if-absent only (never fix drift).
  - **Answer (producer): "2. A"** — non-destructive reconcile, preserve custom entries.
- **Q3: Should new projects get the routines by default?**
  - Options: (a) also update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set); (b) skill-only.
  - **Answer (producer): "3. A"** — template updated so every new project provisions the three routines at 07:00/08:00/09:00 high (`wl init` code path unchanged).

# Worktree Module-Resolution Isolation — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

Two documentation gaps exist: `AGENTS.md` (global and repo copies) contains a
dangling link to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, and the existing isolation
doc lacks a cross-reference to the node-modules-verification doc. This task
produces the final, authoritative documentation on how worktree module
resolution works and repairs all references.

## Users

- **Agents** running the implement workflow: they need one authoritative doc
  explaining the supported setup and the failure signatures to recognise.
- **Producers** reviewing `in_review` items: they need trust in the gate result
  (green means correct, red names the change).
- **Contributors** debugging stale-`dist` false-reds: they need the failure
  signature and the sanctioned refresh mechanism documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New doc created.** `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` documents: (a) the
   module-resolution order in a worktree (node_modules symlink/link farm,
   `@worklog/shared` → main vs worktree `packages/shared`, `main`/`exports` →
   `dist`), (b) the supported way to make `packages/shared` changes visible
   (link farm from SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO), and (c) the stale-dist failure
   signature (e.g. the `spy never called` false red).
2. **AGENTS.md links fixed.** All references to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
   in `AGENTS.md` and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` resolve to an existing file (absolute
   path or correct relative path).
3. **Cross-reference added.** `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`
   links to the new isolation doc.
4. **Constraints stated.** The implement skill's `npm install`-in-worktree ban
   and the no-writes-through-node_modules constraint are stated in the isolation
   doc.
5. **Validation passes.** Markdown link checks and the full project test suite
   pass with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Worktree isolation:** all changes must happen in an `implement.py` worktree.
  Do not edit from the main checkout.
- **No `npm install`** in the worktree (writes through the symlink corrupt the
  main checkout's `node_modules`).
- **Markdown links** must resolve from every document's perspective.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Link portability:** `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is symlinked to SorraAgents'
  `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`. An absolute path to ContextHub's doc will not be
  portable. **Mitigation:** use an absolute path to the specific user's
  ContextHub checkout (the link is only readable, not served to others).
- **Scope creep:** the doc already exists and is comprehensive; do not rewrite
  it. Only add cross-references and fix links.
- **Stale SorraAgents doc:** SorraAgents has its own shorter version of the doc
  at `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`. The AGENTS.md link currently resolves
  to it. **Decision:** the link should point to ContextHub's more comprehensive
  version; verify the implement skill doesn't also link to the SorraAgents copy.

## Existing State

- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` already exists with substantial content
  (worktrees, sync temp worktrees, guards, filesystem-walk races, main-checkout
  deletions).
- `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` exists but does not
  cross-reference the isolation doc.
- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` line 40 has `[docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md](docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md)` —
  a relative link that resolves from the repo root but not from the global
  install location.
- `AGENTS.md` in this repo root and `templates/AGENTS.md` do not currently link
  to the isolation doc (the task is about fixing existing dangling links).

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVLK2JNB002E9JQ** — Worktree tests resolve `@worklog/shared` to the main
  checkout's stale dist (the root cause of the problem this docs the fix for).
- **SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO** — SorraAgents item delivering the link-farm mechanism
  (the resolution fix; blocked-by).
- **WL-0MVWK20DK004TQZM** — Recurrence: `packages/shared` wiped from main checkout.
- **WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2** — Worktree node_modules verification (related doc).
- **WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO** — Verify persist write-detection regression tests
  (the `spy never called` false red example).

## Appendix

No clarifying questions — the work item description and related work provide
sufficient detail for implementation.

## Plan review findings (2026-11-02)

Effort/risk pre-check: **Small / Low** (below the planning threshold), so the
plan session reviewed the existing content instead of decomposing it. Review
outcome: **three open questions block completion** — see below. The item is
left at `intake_complete`, awaiting producer answers.

### Corrected existing state (verified during review)

- **`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` does not exist in this repository.** The global agent
  file `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to
  `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`; it is installed by
  **SorraAgents'** `scripts/install_pi.sh` (ContextHub has no such script).
  ContextHub `AGENTS.md` line 3 claims the install comes from "this
  repository's `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`" — inaccurate for ContextHub, and out of
  scope here unless the producer wants it corrected in this item.
- **Nothing to repair in ContextHub `AGENTS.md` / `templates/AGENTS.md`.**
  Neither contains a reference to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, so the
  "dangling link" exists only in the SorraAgents copy of the global file (its
  relative link is dangling for a reader of `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, while
  resolving fine inside the SorraAgents checkout).
- **ContextHub `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`** (~230 lines) covers
  implementation worktrees, sync temp worktrees, hook guards, main-checkout
  deletion detection/recovery and repo-wide-walk races, but has **no**
  module-resolution section.
- **`docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`** has no link
  to the isolation doc (AC3 confirmed outstanding).
- **No markdown link checker exists in ContextHub** — `package.json` has no
  link/lint script and no doc-link test covers `docs/dev/*.md`. AC5's
  "Markdown link checks" therefore needs either one documented manual command
  or a small script/test added by the item.
- **AC4 constraints:** the `npm install`-in-worktree ban is already stated in
  isolation doc §1; the "no writes through `node_modules`" rule is only
  implied ("writes pass through the symlink and corrupt the shared tree"), not
  stated as a constraint.
- **AC1(b) mechanism does not exist yet:** `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` is still
  `open` / `plan_complete`, and `implement.py` today only provides
  `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (plus nested workspace symlinks) — there is no
  link farm. Documentation would describe a workflow that cannot be followed
  yet.

### AC coverage review

| AC | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| AC1(a) resolution order | Ready | Main checkout's `node_modules/@worklog/shared` → `../../packages/shared`; `main`/`exports` → `./dist/*.js` (verified in `packages/shared/package.json`) |
| AC1(b) link-farm setup | **Blocked** | Depends on `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` (Q2) |
| AC1(c) stale-dist signature | Ready | "spy never called" false red — WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO |
| AC2 link repair | **Blocked** | Cross-repo target + authoritative-doc decision (Q1, Q3) |
| AC3 cross-reference | Ready | Small edit |
| AC4 constraints stated | Ready | Small edit |
| AC5 validation | Ready, with gap | No link checker exists; item must add one or document a manual check |

### OPEN QUESTION 1 — scope / repo split (producer, blocking)

AC2 spans two repositories: `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` lives in the SorraAgents

   responsibility (AC6).

   `DisplayRow`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`,
   `MouseDragState`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseAction`. **Internal** (declared in
   the new modules, exported from them for sibling use, but *not* re-exported by
   the barrel, because no external consumer imports them): `KeyAction`,
   `HelpIconRow`, `NoteEditAction`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`,
   `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution`, `ViewMode`, `MIN_META_SHARE`,
   `MAX_META_SHARE`.
   *(Plan-time correction, 2026-10-30: the guarded symbol set is re-derived
from the live import scan — 66 symbols are imported by the 36 consumer
files. Every symbol listed as internal below is imported by no external
consumer, so parent AC2 requires it to stay module-private.)*

   exported from `./worklist.js`, no worklist module imports the barrel at
   runtime, no new cycle, all modules ≤1,000 lines (AC4, AC1, AC2).

   `packages/herdr` suite passes with **no test-file changes** (AC3, AC9).

   `formatItemLine` reference needs the new home (deferred there if format has

# Split worklist TUI loop into context and handlers

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 6 of 7 (the hard part).

## Target outcome

`runWorklistTui` (currently lines 5581–7899, ~2,319 lines of nested closures over
one mutable context) becomes a thin orchestrator over named handler modules,
with a **single interface-typed context object owned by one module** and passed
explicitly to handler functions — no state duplication and no class-based
controller rewrite (parent constraint).

## Scope (measured closure groups inside `runWorklistTui`)

| New module | Contents | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.tui-context.ts` | The context interface + factory: `opts`, `termSize`, `items`, `state`, `renderer`, `inputActive`, view flags (`formState`, `preFormMode`, `preHelpMode`, `helpScrollOffset`, `shipItDialog`, `podcastNotice`, `blockedNotice`), freeze/sprint flags, dispose hooks. Single owner of the mutable context (AC5) | ~250 |
| `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` | Pane gate, agent tracker, live event subscriptions, pane-marker apply/refresh/batching, metadata blocker resolution + cache (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8), freeze-state refresh, review-queue sprint state | ~560 |
| `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` | Non-blocking sync status notice (F3 — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N), `cleanup`, `closeEventSubscriber`, `doRefresh` (single-flight + pending), `doSync`, `openShipItDialog` / `openShipItDialogGuarded` | ~480 |
| `worklist.tui-input.ts` | `dispatchMouse`, `handleKeyInput`, streaming stdin decode (`onData` + `KeypressDecoder`), `readKeyFile`/`writeKeyFile`, `buildHelpEntries`/`buildHelpIconLegend` | ~800 |
| `worklist.tui-render.ts` | `render`, `onResize`, `TaskScheduler` wiring, hydrator runner, resume poll, db-change watch, and the `runWorklistTui` orchestrator that constructs the context and registers handlers | ~570 |

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `runWorklistTui` is retained at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical
   signature and return type (`Promise<WorkItem | undefined>`), implemented as a
   thin orchestrator (context construction + handler registration + teardown);
   no module and no single exported function carries the former 2,319-line body
   (AC1).
2. Every new module ≤1,000 lines with a responsibility doc comment; the TUI-local
   sub-banners (metadata-panel dependency blockers — WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8,
   review-queue depth indicator, event-driven window status — WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ,
   non-blocking sync status notice — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N, mouse event dispatch —
   WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ AC2–AC6, streaming stdin decode — WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH,
   consolidated scheduler loop — WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP, hydrator —
   WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI) and their inline work-item ids move verbatim (AC6).
3. **Single context, explicit passing.** The context type is declared once in
   `worklist.tui-context.ts`; handler modules receive it as a parameter and
   never re-declare a mutable field it already owns. `WorkItemListState`
   remains a single instance created by the orchestrator (AC5); the split guard's
   single-owner gate stays green.
4. Lifecycle ordering is preserved exactly: event-subscription setup, pane gate,
   refresh single-flight/pending, scheduler ticks, hydrator, resume poll and
   teardown order are unchanged — verified by the unmodified
   `worklist-integration.test.ts`, `worklist-active-pane-marker.test.ts`,
   `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts`, `worklist-consolidated-refresh.test.ts`,
   `worklist-watch.test.ts`, `worklist-inflight.test.ts`,
   `worklist-sync-notice.test.ts` and `worklist.test.ts` TUI blocks (AC3).
5. Split guard, `tsc --noEmit`/build and the full `packages/herdr` suite pass;
   no new cycle; no runtime barrel import (AC4, AC9).
6. Docs updated: `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block, `onPaneFocused`
   and `isInputActive` references at ~1619 and ~1781, and the ~1829 "task
   registration in `worklist.ts`" note), `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`,
   `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — all path references resolve
   to the new modules.
7. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
   → Owned by this slice: `WorkItemListState` and the extracted TUI context each live in exactly one module and no mutable state is duplicated.

## Minimal implementation

1. Introduce `worklist.tui-context.ts` with the context interface and factory;
   move the `opts`/state/flag declarations into it **without** changing any
   initial value or ordering.
2. Extract `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` (subscriptions, pane markers, blockers,
   freeze/sprint state) as functions taking the context.
3. Extract `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` (`doRefresh`/`doSync`/ship-it dialog/notice/
   cleanup) as functions taking the context.
4. Extract `worklist.tui-input.ts` (`handleKeyInput`/`dispatchMouse`/`onData`/
   key-file IO/help entries) as functions taking the context.
5. Extract `worklist.tui-render.ts` (render/resize/scheduler/hydrator/resume
   poll/db-change watch) and reduce `runWorklistTui` to orchestration.
   Land steps 1–5 as **separate commits**, each with the full suite green, so a
   behavioural regression is attributable to one closure group.
6. Run guard + build + suite; update docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-context.ts` — new (single context owner).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-handlers.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-refresh.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-input.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-render.ts` — new (holds the orchestrator).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — re-exports `runWorklistTui`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — consumer; must compile unchanged.
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md` and the five `docs/dev/*` files listed above.

## Constraints

- No class-based controller conversion, no state duplication, no reordering of
  lifecycle steps, no changed defaults or timings.
- The context is interface-typed and passed explicitly; closures may become
  module functions but must not change observable behaviour.
- No barrel/`index.ts` imports inside the new modules; no test edits.

## Dependencies

- `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J` — refactor guard (test-first).
- `WL-0MVND6DHH008R3LG` — constants/types/layout.
- `WL-0MVND6F9V004IQ3V` — state/navigation.
- `WL-0MVND6H5Q006YO9Z` — presentation.
- `WL-0MVND6J090041GWK` — input pipeline (key/mouse handlers move with it).
- `WL-0MVND6KVF0089878` — renderer/commands (the loop dispatches through them).

## Deliverables

Five TUI modules with a thin `runWorklistTui`, guard + full suite green, docs
updated.

   → Owned by this slice: `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for every production `worklist*.ts` module, including the barrel, and no exported function carries the former TUI body.
8. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./worklist.js` by another module remains exported from that
   exact path with identical types and values, so the 36 importing files
   (2 production consumers + 34 test files, of which 24 are `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites) compile with no import-path edits. 66 distinct symbols are imported
   today; the barrel
   re-exports **only symbols consumers actually use** — unused exports stay
   internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer decision, parent
   WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q2 → "A, but only re-export symbols that are
   actually used").
   → Owned by this slice: the barrel re-exports exactly the symbols consumers import and the 36 importing files (`index.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, 34 test files) compile unchanged.
9. **Testing/validation criterion:** the extracted modules are covered by the
   existing, unmodified `worklist*.test.ts` suites; the split adds no behaviour
   of its own, so no new assertions are required. Validation includes
   `tsc --noEmit`/build success, no new circular-import report, and a line-count
   check asserting every `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` production module is
   ≤1,000 lines.
   → Owned by this slice: the guard covers the extracted modules, `tsc --noEmit`/build succeeds, no new circular-import report appears and the line-count check asserts every module ≤1,000 lines.
10. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
   → Owned by this slice: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` and every `docs/dev/*` reference resolve to the new module paths.
11. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
   → Owned by this slice: the full project test suite passes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Rewrite `worklist.ts` as the barrel; remove the 23 unused exports from the
   public surface (they remain exported by their owning modules only if a sibling
   module needs them; otherwise they become module-private).
2. Re-generate nothing in the baseline (it is frozen); only clear the allowlist
   in the guard config and update the `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST_CEILING` expectation.
3. Run the import scan to prove the exported set equals the consumed set; attach
   the output to the completion comment.
4. Update `packages/herdr/README.md` module block and the five `docs/dev/*`
   references; add a one-paragraph "module map" note to the README.
5. Run the guard, build, and the full suite; record the final `wc -l` table in
   the completion comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — thin barrel (≤250 lines).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` — empty allowlist.
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — allowlist config for worklist.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — module map and prose references.
- `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md`, `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`,
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`,
  `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`,
  `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`,
  `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — path references.

## Constraints

- Move-only overall: this child deletes re-exports, it does not change any

- No test-file rewrites; the guard file added in `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J` is the only new test.
- The two oversized test suites are handled by their own follow-up children, not

## Dependencies

Thin barrel, empty-allowlist guard, module map docs, final line-count table, full

Discovered during plan review of WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (discovered-from:WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ).

Producer finding from the machine-hygiene session (2025-10-21): propose_remediations() in skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py emits a renice action for every large RSS contributor under memory/swap pressure without inspecting the target's current nice value. In the observed run every proposed target was already at nice 19 or 0, and the targets included two live test suites (AI_Hell vitest, tce-the-rising browser suite) - the action would have slowed active work.

Suggested fix (from producer): skip renice when min(nice) over the target pids is already >= the proposed nice value, and surface the current nice value in the action's reason/target so the operator can see why an action is proposed or suppressed.

Note: this is deliberately separate from the duplication fix in WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (dedupe + single render); this item is the semantic safety change and needs process-nice collection support.

Scope: scanning niceness (/proc/<pid>/stat field 19) for target pids, suppressing no-op renicces, and tests for both suppressed and emitted cases. Related: skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py (propose_remediations), metrics collection if nice must be collected centrally.

Goal: a local-only pane whose prompt exceeds the local provider's context ceiling should degrade predictably instead of stalling or failing, and the reason should be visible to the operator.

Observed problem: the local provider rejects a local-only request when the projected prompt exceeds ~38k tokens warm, or ~25k on a cold prefix. Because the pane is labelled local-only the proxy refuses the local route, and the work is not processed on the local slot. Evidence in this deployment's route logs (.worklog/local-route.log, 697 turns across 5 roots): 49 turns route remote with fallbackReason resident_prefix_insufficient and 44 with large_context_bypass; 72 turns actually served local. The thresholds and the exact refusal behaviour (hard error vs silent fallback) live in the external llama-proxy (LP project), not in this repo - confirm before designing the fix.

Open design questions to settle in plan:
- Is the correct behaviour a fallback to remote for over-threshold requests, an explicit hard error surfaced to the operator, or pre-dispatch routing (choose remote-ok when the projected context exceeds the ceiling)?
- Where is the projected context size knowable? The pi extension sees the outgoing request (before_provider_headers), the dispatcher does not.
- Interaction with WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX (low priority -> local-only): over-threshold low-priority work must not become unprocessable.

ACs:
- [ ] Reproduce the failure deterministically (unit test or scripted proxy stub) for a prompt above 38k warm and above 25k cold, recording the observed proxy response headers.
- [ ] Document the confirmed thresholds and the refusal semantics (hard error vs fallback) in docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md.
- [ ] A local-only request over the ceiling produces a deterministic, observable outcome - no silent stall - with the reason recorded in .worklog/local-route.log.
- [ ] The chosen mitigation (fallback, hard error, or pre-dispatch routing) is covered by tests on both sides of each threshold.
- [ ] Operators can see over-threshold refusals without reading raw JSONL (documented query/ or herdr view).
- [ ] Full test suite green.

# tree_coverage AC extraction ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

discovered-from:WL-0MVGB23MM004X501

## Status: partially delivered elsewhere (scope narrowed at plan time)

ACs 1–4 of the original brief are already satisfied in the **SorraAgents**
repository, which owns `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` and the plan/intake skill
docs (ContextHub's `skill/` directory is a symlink to `~/.pi/agent/skills`,
installed from SorraAgents):

- `26cc220b` — **SA-0MUYHHG1Y0040PPV**: ordered-list AC extraction (`1. `,
  `1) `) alongside `- ` / `+ ` bullets.
- `7b1aeece2` — **SA-0MVO7R2WU0058RNJ**: nested-detail exclusion (a marker
  indented deeper than the first AC marker is detail, not an AC), decision
  parity between numbered and bulleted AC lists, and fail-closed behaviour when
  an `## Acceptance Criteria` section parses to zero ACs
  (`recommendation: "stop"` plus an explicit warning instead of a vacuous
  `proceed`).
- Evidence: `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` —
  `test_numbered_acs_extracted`, `test_paren_numbered_acs_extracted`,
  `test_mixed_bullets_and_numbers_preserve_document_order`,
  `test_bullet_list_behaviour_unchanged`, `test_empty_section_returns_empty`,
  `test_numbered_and_bulleted_acs_produce_same_recommendation`,
  `test_unparseable_ac_section_fails_closed`.

Duplicate check (plan, 2026-11-02): searched the ContextHub worklog for
`tree_coverage`, `numbered` and `acceptance criteria` — no other ContextHub item
covers this gap; the SA items above are the implementation records.

## Remaining gap

The tooling now accepts numbered AC lists, but neither the **plan** nor the
**intake** skill tells an author which AC formats the coverage tooling
recognises. Contributors still normalise AC lists to `- ` bullets by hand
(WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS, WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) or document the "limitation"
(WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7) because the capability is undocumented.

## Desired outcome

1. `skill/plan/SKILL.md` states the AC formats the coverage tooling recognises,
   in the guidance that already covers AC validation and AC coverage review.
2. `skill/intake/SKILL.md` states the same formats in its AC list template
   guidance.
3. The documented list matches `extract_acceptance_criteria` behaviour: `- `
   and `+ ` bullets; `1. ` and `1) ` ordered items; interleaved bullets and
   numbers in document order; nested (deeper-indented) markers treated as
   detail rather than ACs; wrapped continuation lines belonging to the
   preceding AC.
4. Documentation records the fail-closed behaviour: an `## Acceptance Criteria`
   section that parses to zero ACs stops the coverage review instead of passing
   vacuously.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` lists the AC formats recognised by the coverage tooling
  (`- `, `+ `, `1. `, `1) `) in its AC validation/coverage guidance.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` lists the same supported AC formats in its AC list
  template guidance.
- Both docs state that nested/deeper-indented markers are detail rather than
  ACs, and that an AC section parsing to zero ACs fails the coverage review
  closed.
- The documented wording matches the implementation and its tests, citing
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` and
  `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`.
- The change is documentation-only: `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` and its
  tests are unmodified by this item.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — AC validation (`Editing rules & safety`) and AC
  coverage review guidance.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — AC list template guidance.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — reference implementation (read-only here).
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — evidence for the documented
  behaviour (read-only here).

## Out of scope (already delivered — historical brief)

Original problem: `extract_acceptance_criteria` collected only `- ` / `+ `
bullets inside the `## Acceptance Criteria` section, so work items with a
numbered list (`1. …`, `2. …`) yielded an empty AC set and
`run_coverage_review` reported `fully_covered: true` / `recommendation:
proceed` with zero parent ACs — the gate passed vacuously.

Original acceptance criteria (all satisfied by the SA items above):

- Numbered AC lists (`1. …`) and bullet lists (`- …`) are both extracted by
  `extract_acceptance_criteria`, with matching output for equivalent content.
- A numbered AC list in a work item description produces a non-zero
  `parent_acs` count from `run_coverage_review`.
- An `## Acceptance Criteria` section that parses to zero ACs no longer returns
  `recommendation: proceed` silently — it is surfaced as a conflict or explicit
  warning in the review result.
- Unit tests cover: numbered list, bullet list, mixed list, empty AC section,
  and the zero-AC stop/warn behaviour.

## Notes

- Workaround for items already affected: normalise the AC list to `- ` bullets
  (wording unchanged). No longer required for coverage purposes, but still the
  most readable form.
- Landing repository: **SorraAgents** — skill docs are authored there and
  installed into `~/.pi/agent/skills`; a ContextHub worktree cannot modify the
  symlinked skill tree, so verification must run from a SorraAgents worktree.

# Decompose `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (4,284 lines)

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6 (Refactor: decompose
`packages/herdr/src/index.ts` god module).
**Status:** follow-up, deliberately **outside** that epic.

## Why this is not part of the index.ts epic

The index.ts split (WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6) is a move-only refactor whose
behaviour gate is that `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts` and
`fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` stay **byte-identical**. Decomposing
`index.test.ts` inside the same epic would erase that signal, so it is filed
here as a separate item (plan decision Q3 → A).

## Target outcome

`packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (4,284 lines, measured 2026-11-05) is split
into cohesive test modules grouped by the production module they exercise
(commands, args, pane-capture, background, interactive/resolvers,
downtime-deps, settings/main) or another agreed grouping, with no test cases
lost and no production-code changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wc -l` reports ≤ 1,000 lines for every resulting `index*.test.ts` module.
- The total number of test cases (`it(`/`test(`) and assertions is unchanged before and after; no test is deleted, skipped or weakened.
- No production module changes; `packages/herdr` build and full test suite pass.
- Shared fixtures/helpers are extracted into a single helper module rather than duplicated across the new files.
- The split guard's line-ceiling gate excludes test files (asserted explicitly) so test sizes are not policed by the production ceiling.

## Baseline metrics (measured 2026-11-05 on `dev` @ 33bd3a07)

AC1/AC2 are verified against these numbers before and after the split:

- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — **4,284 lines**; 34 top-level
  `describe` blocks (41 including nested); **226 `it(...)` declarations** plus
  one `it.each` table with 4 parameterised cases (**231 executed cases**);
  **400 `expect(...)` assertions**; 4 `beforeEach`, 15 `afterEach`.
- No `it.skip`, `it.only` or `test(` call exists today; none may be added.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` — 484 lines (already under the
  ceiling and otherwise untouched apart from the AC5 assertion).

## Grouping map (inventory, measured 2026-11-05)

| Proposed module | Describes it takes (start line → length) | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `index.args.test.ts` | `buildSendToPiArgs` (72→103), `buildRunInPaneArgs` (175→100), item-tab anchor variants (275→43, 318→69), pane-id capture flag (3436→26), request priority (4005→24) | ~365 |
| `index.interactive.test.ts` | `extractWorkItemId` (387→17), `resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId` (404→30), `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` (434→116), `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver` (550→93), `closeInteractiveTabRootPane` (643→123), `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority` (4111→86), operator-dispatch chain (4197→87) | ~552 |
| `index.commands.test.ts` | `stripCommandPrefix` (766→116), shortcuts.json routing (882→119), `routeCommand` (1001→56), `stripAgentPromptPrefix` (1057→48) | ~339 |
| `index.pane-capture.test.ts` | `parsePaneIdFile` (3462→17), `capturePaneIdFromFile` (3479→85) | ~128 |
| `index.background.test.ts` | `buildBackgroundLogPath` (3629→14), `spawnBackgroundShell` (3643→64), `formatBackgroundFailure` (3707→44), `spawnBackgroundPi` (3751→57), `spawnBackgroundPi` priority env (4029→82) | ~261 |
| `index.settings.test.ts` | `configureWorklogTarget` (1105→108) | ~108 |
| `index.downtime-deps*.test.ts` | `createDowntimeDeps` (1213→**1,407**), `host-wide audit admission` (2620→380), `recordDispatch` (3000→161), `recordError` (3161→37), `recordDispatchFailure` (3198→83), `getDueScheduledPrompt` (3281→89), `recordScheduledPromptTrigger` (3370→66), `rotation wiring` (3564→65) | ~2,288 |
| `index.stalled-work-wiring.test.ts` | `stalled-work production wiring` (3808→197) | ~197 |

Consequences of the inventory:

- The single `createDowntimeDeps` describe (**1,407 lines**) cannot move into one
  module under AC1. It must be subdivided by its nested describes (or at a
  shared-setup seam) so that the downtime-deps family lands in at least three
  modules ≤ 1,000 lines each, with `createDowntimeDeps` setup in
  `index.fixtures.ts`.
- The 2,288-line downtime-deps family is the bulk of the work; the remaining
  ~1,750 lines split cleanly by production module.

## Minimal implementation

1. Inventory done — see **Grouping map** above (verify it still matches before
   moving code; the file grows over time).
2. Extract shared mocks/fixtures to `packages/herdr/src/index.fixtures.ts`
   (suite-wide `beforeEach`/`afterEach` host-CPU pinning, `makeInteractiveAnchorDeps`,
   `loadInteractiveAnchorHelpers`, `createDowntimeDeps` stubs and other shared
   arrange helpers).
3. Move blocks into `index.<concern>.test.ts` files; keep imports pointing at
   `./index.js` (the barrel) so the public-surface contract keeps being tested.
   Import a concrete `./index.<slice>.js` path only where the barrel does not
   expose the symbol.
4. Add the explicit AC5 assertion to `index.split-guard.test.ts`: test/fixture
   files are excluded from the production line ceiling (today that exclusion is
   only implicit in `productionModules()` filtering).
5. Update `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/dispatcher-anchor-family.ts`
   `KNOWN_CONSUMER_FILES` (it names `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, and
   `findBarrelConsumers(...)` is asserted to equal the list exactly) to name the
   module that keeps the `DispatcherAnchorDeps` type imports.
6. Verify with `/skill:test` scoped to `packages/herdr`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — source of the split (4,284 lines).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.*.test.ts` — new test modules.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.fixtures.ts` — shared fixtures (new).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` — receives the AC5 assertion.
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/dispatcher-anchor-family.ts` — frozen
  consumer list update (test tooling, not a production module).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate `describe` blocks, helpers and imports; test names and
  assertions stay byte-identical. No test deleted, skipped, renamed or weakened.
- **Test-only change;** must not alter production behaviour or public surface.
  `packages/herdr/src/index.split-baseline.json` is a frozen contract — never
  regenerate it to make a gate green.
- **Fixture naming matters.** `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`'s
  `isTestOrFixture()` recognises only `*.test.ts` and `*.fixtures.ts`, while
  `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN` (`/^index(\.[\w-]+)?\.ts$/`) *does* match
  `index.test-helpers.ts` — so a helper named `index.test-helpers.ts` would be
  treated as an index-family **production** module and held to the 1,000-line
  ceiling plus the single-declaration/single-callsite gates. Use
  `index.fixtures.ts`, matching the existing `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` /
  `host-dispatch-budget.fixtures.ts` convention.
- **Do not pollute the production size gate.** `INDEX_SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` and
  `INDEX_SPLIT_ALLOWLIST_CEILING` are `['index.ts']` and shrink-only; no split
  test module may be added to them.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf test groups first, keeping the
  tree green between moves; run the scoped suite after each module.
- **Guard divergence is deliberate.** The sibling test-decomposition items
  (`WL-0MVHURHZI000CS5L`, `WL-0MVHUU096008OQSW`) extend their split guard to
  *police* `worklist*.test.ts` at ≤1,000 lines; this item's AC5 requires the
  opposite for the index family (test files explicitly **excluded** from the
  production ceiling). Do not harmonise the two.
- **No production-split prerequisite.** `index.ts` is still 2,072 lines and
  remains on the shrink-only allowlist; its epic (WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6) is
  deleted, so this item is independent. Moves must not touch `index.ts` itself.

## Related work

- WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6 — parent epic (deleted; the split shipped as separate
  production modules and `index.ts` remains on the allowlist).
- WL-0MVHURHZI000CS5L — decompose `worklist.test.ts` (7,073 lines), blocked.
- WL-0MVHUU096008OQSW — decompose `worklist-mouse.test.ts` (1,132 lines), blocked.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` / `index.split-baseline.json` —
  the structural gates that must stay green.

## Appendix: planning questions, findings and answers

**Duplicate check.** `wl search "index.test.ts"`,
`wl search "decompose test god file split module herdr"` and
`wl search "index.test.ts decompose split test"` performed 2026-11-05. The only
overlapping items are the sibling *worklist* test decompositions (different
files, no AC overlap) and this item; no completed item satisfies these ACs.
**No overlapping completed item found** — proceed.

- **Q: Is `index.test-helpers.ts` (named in the original Key Files) a safe
  fixture name?** Answer (plan, verified against
  `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/{scan,index-family}.ts` with `tsx`):
  **no** — it matches `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN` and is not recognised by
  `isTestOrFixture()`, so it would be gated as production. Accepted naming:
  `index.fixtures.ts`. Evidence: `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN.test('index.test-helpers.ts') === true`,
  `isTestOrFixture('index.test-helpers.ts') === false`.
- **Q: Does the line-count in the title/description still hold?** Answer
  (measured): no — the file is 4,284 lines, not 3,990. Title and description
  corrected; counts recorded under **Baseline metrics**.
- **Q: Does the item stay clear of the frozen production gates?** Answer
  (verified): yes, provided the split does not add test modules to the
  allowlist, does not regenerate `index.split-baseline.json`, and updates the
  *test-tooling* `KNOWN_CONSUMER_FILES` list, which currently names
  `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and is asserted by exact equality.
- **Q: Is `claim` a real group in this file (the original description listed
  it)?** Answer (inventory): no — `claim` coverage lives in `claim.test.ts`;
  removed from the grouping list.
- **Decision (scope sizing / phasing):** no children are created and no
  phasing is needed — this is a single move-only deliverable. If the 1,407-line
  `createDowntimeDeps` describe proves unmanageable during implementation,
  `implement` may create children then, test-first (AC5 assertion → fixture
  module → downtime-deps sub-split → remaining concerns).
- **Decision (residual barrel test file):** `index.test.ts` is expected to be
  removed once its describes are distributed; the public-surface contract is
  preserved by the split-guard baseline and by the new modules importing
  `./index.js`. A thin residual `index.test.ts` is acceptable if a home is
  needed for file-level setup.
- **Note (effort/risk provenance):** the autoplan pre-check ran
  `effort-and-risk` with its zeroed placeholder payload (`o=m=p=0`) and wrote
  `Extra Small`/`Low`; step 8 replaced both fields with a real three-point
  estimate (see the effort/risk fields and the `effort_and_risk_skill`
  comment).

## Goal

Move the store's connection-adjacent concerns — schema DDL/versioning/additive repair and the metadata / export-watermark / delta-sync read-write helpers — into `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/schema.ts` and `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/metadata.ts`, leaving the constructor and connection open logic in the façade.

Third vertical slice: modules + façade delegation + guard suite + build + tests + docs in one deliverable.

## Scope

- `persistent-store/schema.ts` — `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `REQUIRED_COLUMNS`, `initializeSchema`, `repairRequiredColumns`, `isSchemaInitialised`, `detectFtsAvailable`.
- `persistent-store/metadata.ts` — `getMetadata`/`setMetadata`/`getAllMetadata`, `getLastExportTimestamps`/`setLastExportTimestamps`, `getDeltaSyncMetadata`/`setDeltaSyncMetadata`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistent-store/schema.ts` contains `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `REQUIRED_COLUMNS`, `initializeSchema`, `repairRequiredColumns`, `isSchemaInitialised` and `detectFtsAvailable`, moved verbatim (identical DDL strings, identical `PRAGMA table_info` logic, identical FTS5 probe), each taking an injected `StoreContext`/`db` handle, with a responsibility header comment.
2. The schema version constant and the required-column table are defined **once** in `schema.ts` and consumed by the façade by import — no duplicated DDL or column list remains in `persistent-store.ts`.
3. `persistent-store/metadata.ts` contains the metadata store, the last-export-timestamp pair and the delta-sync metadata pair, moved verbatim with identical keys and identical parsing/`Number` coercion behaviour, with a responsibility header comment.
4. The read-only open contract is unchanged: a read-only open still runs **no** schema/FTS DDL on an already-initialised store (`packages/shared/src/database-readonly.test.ts` passes untouched).
5. The additive repair path is unchanged: `repairRequiredColumns` still ALTERs only missing columns and reports the same `RequiredColumn[]` result (`packages/shared/src/audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts` and `database-dedup.test.ts` pass untouched).
6. All 11 public exports remain importable from `./persistent-store.js`; `packages/shared/src/persistent-store-architecture.test.ts` stays green.
7. Move-only: no SQL, ordering, error-message or public-signature change; no existing test file modified.
8. `npm run build:shared` and the changed-scope test gate (test skill) pass.
9. `packages/shared/README.md` Package Structure lists `schema.ts` and `metadata.ts` with their single responsibility.

## Minimal implementation

1. Cut `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `RequiredColumn`, `REQUIRED_COLUMNS`, `isSchemaInitialised`, `detectFtsAvailable`, `initializeSchema`, `repairRequiredColumns` into `schema.ts` as functions over the context; keep `initializeSchema` returning `void` and `repairRequiredColumns` returning `RequiredColumn[]` exactly as today.
2. Cut `DbMetadata`, the metadata CRUD and both watermark pairs into `metadata.ts` as context-taking functions; keep the class methods as one-line delegates so no call site inside the façade changes in this child.
3. Confirm the constructor still performs the same sequence (open → read-only check → schema init when writable/initialised → FTS probe) — sequence changes are out of bounds.

# Canonical full suite excludes `packages/` tests (tui 30 + shared 13 files)

*Discovered from WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (canonical suite root-level `tests/` coverage).* That item closed the `tests/` gap by replacing the two narrow `suiteCommands` with the umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`. It deliberately kept its scope to `tests/`, so the `packages/` gap remains.

**Note:** file counts have grown since the work item was created — `packages/tui` now has 30 test files (was 22) and `packages/shared` has 13 (was 12). The `packages/herdr` count is 129, unchanged. Repository total: 453 test files (up from 440).

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` (the single source of full-suite evidence for `/skill:test --type full`, the ship release gate and audit F3) resolves only to `tests/`. Tracked test files by location:

| Location | Test files | In canonical suite? |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/` | 277 | Yes (since WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR) |
| `packages/herdr` | 129 | No — producer decision (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); opt-in `--type herdr` / `--group herdr` |
| `packages/tui` | 30 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| `packages/shared` | 13 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| **Repository total** | **453** | **277** |

`packages/tui/**/*.test.ts` (30 files, all under `packages/tui/extensions/`) and `packages/shared/**/*.test.ts` (13 files) run under a bare `npx vitest` / CI but are referenced by neither `suiteCommands` nor any cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths, so no gate can execute or cache-evidence them. (Note: a `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`.)

## Goal

Every `packages/` test file is either executed by the canonical full suite (or a cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths), or has an explicit documented exclusion with a rationale — the same standard WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR applied to `tests/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.pi/test-config.json` covers `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` tests (in `suiteCommands`, or as named `groups` entries wired to their paths so `implement.py finish` selects them), or each exclusion is documented with a rationale in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`.
- A full `/skill:test` run (`python3 <test-skill>/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --json`) reports the newly covered files as executed, with the executed-file count recorded in the work item.
- Any failures surfaced by the change are triaged into `test-failure` work items.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the "Test gates" section is shared, not duplicated) carries the updated coverage table (files executed / excluded / why) and the measured runtime.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Evidence-path constraint:** full-suite evidence for the audit resolves `--type full` from `suiteCommands` only; a new `groups.*` entry alone does not satisfy a "full suite passes" AC (see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` → "Cache evidence scope").
- **Vitest filters are substring matches** on the repository-relative path, so `packages/shared` / `packages/tui` can be selected by positional filters (`-- tests` umbrella does not cover them; `-- packages` would also pull in `packages/herdr`, which is excluded by producer decision).
- **Do not re-litigate the herdr decision** (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix; `groups.herdr` added by WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN).
- Measure runtime before/after with the test-skill runner (`run_tests.py`), not ad-hoc `npx vitest`.
- Beware the `run_tests.py --suite node` trap: that suite name resolves through the legacy convention path (`tests/{unit,node,cli}`) and ignores `suiteCommands`; use the default `--suite all` for canonical runs.

## Existing state

The canonical suite is a single command: `npm --silent test -- tests` (277 files, ~791 s vitest duration, ~1065 s wall clock). The `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`. There is no group for `packages/shared`.

## Desired change

Add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to the canonical full suite coverage. The simplest approach is to add additional commands to `suiteCommands`:

```jsonc
{
  "suiteCommands": [
    "npm --silent test -- tests",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/shared",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/tui/extensions"
  ]
}
```

This adds two positional filters that are precise: `packages/shared` matches only the 13 shared test files, and `packages/tui/extensions` matches only the 30 tui test files (all under `extensions/`), neither of which would match `packages/herdr`.

Alternatively, create named groups (`shared`, `tui`) and wire them into `suiteCommands` as separate commands — same effect, but with changed-scope selection benefits.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to `suiteCommands` (or create named groups + wire them)
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — update the coverage table and runtime section
- `vitest.config.ts` — no change expected; existing config handles `packages/` correctly

## Related work

- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** — closed the `tests/` coverage gap (umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`); records the OPEN QUESTION that became this item.
- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — herdr package suite excluded by producer decision (won't-fix).
- **WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN** — added `groups.herdr` to `.pi/test-config.json`.
- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** — source of the additional-gap evidence for `packages/tui/extensions/**`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should packages/herdr be included?" — Answer (work item description): No — producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix. Source: work item description.
- Q: "What about the `tui-extensions` group that already exists?" — Answer: It is not wired into `suiteCommands`, so it provides no full-suite gate coverage. The brief proposes wiring it (or creating an equivalent group) into suiteCommands. Source: inspection of `.pi/test-config.json`.
- Q: "File counts have changed since the work item was created — should we update the title?" — Answer: Yes — the title should be updated to reflect current counts (30 + 13, not 22 + 12). Source: `git ls-files` on current tree.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Runtime increase (medium).** Adding 43 files to the canonical suite increases wall-clock. *Mitigation:* measure before/after with `run_tests.py`; `timeoutPerCommand` is 3600 s, so there is headroom.
- **New coverage may surface pre-existing failures (medium).** Neither `packages/tui` nor `packages/shared` has run under the canonical gate, so latent failures could appear. *Mitigation:* triage into `test-failure` items (AC3).
- **Filter precision (low).** `packages/shared` and `packages/tui/extensions` are substring filters; verified against `git ls-files` that they match only the intended 13 + 30 files and not `packages/herdr`. *Assumption:* `packages/tui` has no test files outside `extensions/` (confirmed: 30/30 are under `extensions/`).
- **Scope creep (low).** `packages/herdr` is explicitly out of scope (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); covering it would require re-litigating a closed won't-fix decision. Any further gap (e.g. a new package) becomes a linked work item, not added scope.
- **Assumption:** adding commands to `suiteCommands` (rather than only `groups`) is required, because `--type full` evidence resolves from `suiteCommands` only (evidence-path constraint). A group-only change would not satisfy AC2.
