# Make groupings stable

## Problem statement

When the herdr selection list re-sorts on refresh, items sometimes move from
one group to another even though nothing about them changed materially. This
causes disconcerting movement in the list. The list should only change when
the underlying items change in a material way (e.g. a new key file is added,
or the priority changes). Additionally, items should sort in priority order —
all high items ahead of medium, all medium ahead of low.

## Users

- **Herdr users / producers** who watch the worklist to decide what to work
  on next. A stable list lets them track where work sits; gratuitous movement
  breaks their mental model of the queue.
- **Producers reviewing the in-review queue** who rely on a predictable
  within-group order to find the most important work first.

User story: *As a Herdr user, I want the worklist grouping and ordering to be
a stable function of the items themselves, so that an item only changes
group when its content (key files, priority, stage/status) or the item set
changes — and within each group, high-priority items always rank above
medium, which rank above low.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Group assignment is **content-deterministic**: for a fixed set of items
      with fixed key files / priority / stage / status, the group each item
      lands in is identical regardless of the order in which the items are
      presented to the grouping algorithm (canonical ordering applied before
      the greedy first-fit packing). A transient change such as an
      `updatedAt` timestamp (comment added, audit run) must never change an
      item's group.
- [ ] An item's group membership changes **only** when a material input
      changes: its key files section, its priority, its stage/status, or the
      item set itself (item added/removed). Verified by a stability test
      that perturbs non-material inputs (`updatedAt`, input order) and
      asserts group labels/numbers are unchanged.
- [ ] Within each group (Critical Group N and Group N), items sort by
      **priority first (high → medium → low)**, then by the existing stage
      sub-order (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then by
      id — so all high items appear ahead of all medium items, which appear
      ahead of all low items. The `in_review` 6-bucket comparator already
      sorts priority-first and keeps that behaviour.
- [ ] The change is applied **and kept in sync** in both mirrors: core
      `wl next` / `wl worklist` grouping (`src/commands/grouping.ts`,
      `src/worklist-selection.ts`) and the herdr plugin copy
      (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`); shared grouping tests cover both
      copies.
- [ ] `wl next -n N` and the herdr worklist still emit the canonical section
      order (Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review) with no
      regression in existing grouping/smart-selection behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
      comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Greedy first-fit file-path conflict detection is retained — the change
  makes it order-independent, it does not replace the packing strategy.
- Herdr plugin has zero npm dependencies and cannot import from
  `src/commands/`; the mirror must stay a self-contained pure duplication
  (per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B decision Q2c).
- The always-show-mandatory guarantee of `selectWorkItems`
  (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`) is preserved — grouping only
  reorders and stamps, never filters or drops items.
- Default `maxGroups` of 3 for file-path-based groups is unchanged.

## Existing state

- `regroupWorkItems` (herdr) / `selectBrowseFeed` (core) recompute group
  assignments on every refresh from the merged selection.
- `groupItemsByFilePaths` is a greedy first-fit over items **in input
  order**; the input order fluctuates with `updatedAt` (comment/audit
  churn), so the same item set can pack into different groups across
  refreshes. That is the root cause of the observed group hopping.
- Within-group ordering (`compareGroupableItems`) currently sorts by stage
  sub-order first (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then
  priority; `in_review` items already sort priority-first.

## Desired change

1. Make `groupItemsByFilePaths` (and hence `assignItemGroups`) a pure
   function of the item content: sort/canonicalise the input items by a
   stable content-derived key before greedy packing, so group membership
   depends only on ids, key files, priority and stage/status — not on
   transient ordering.
2. Make priority the **primary** within-group sort key in
   `compareGroupableItems` (both mirrors), keeping the stage sub-order as
   the secondary key.
3. Keep the two mirrors in sync and extend the grouping tests in both
   locations with stability assertions (order perturbation + non-material
   input perturbation must not change group membership or ordering).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — core `groupItemsByFilePaths` / `assignItemGroups` / `compareGroupableItems`; canonicalise input order; priority-first within-group sort.
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — core `selectBrowseFeed` grouping pipeline consuming `assignItemGroups`.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — mirrored plugin copy of the same algorithm; must stay in sync.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems`; input order source feeding `regroupWorkItems` (contract only — no functional change expected unless needed for canonicalisation).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — callers of `regroupWorkItems`.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — core grouping tests; add stability assertions.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — plugin grouping tests; mirror stability assertions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Within-group order change is intentional but observable:** making priority
  the primary within-group sort key changes which item of a group renders
  first (stage sub-order becomes secondary). Existing tests in
  `grouping.test.ts` / `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` that assert the old
  stage-first order must be updated deliberately, not incidentally.
- **Canonicalisation key must be content-derived:** the pre-pack sort key
  (e.g. priority + stage + id) must never include timestamps or insertion
  order, or the instability simply moves to the new key.
- **Assumption — "material change" definition:** key files (the `**Key Files:**`
  section), priority, stage/status, or item-set membership. Description prose
  outside the Key Files section already cannot affect grouping
  (`extractFilePaths` reads only that section) and stays non-material.
- **Scope-creep guard:** out-of-scope opportunities (stable group *labels*
  across renumbering, configurable `maxGroups`) are recorded as related/future
  work, not implemented here.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ — Rewrite `assignItemGroups` + `next.ts` ordering (completed; produced the current grouping spec this item stabilises).
- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW — Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order) (completed; established section order + `regroupWorkItems`).
- WL-0MUY1CSQG007TCYX — actively-worked items derived from `status === 'in-progress'` (affects group membership inputs).
- WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G — in_review priority-first ordering (precedent for priority-first within-group sort).

### Related work (automated report)

Low-relevance automatic matches (find-related): WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C (Bubble
up critical items), WL-0MRSGMTYY0062WFJ (audit-set fail hard), WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9
(needs-producer-review filter) — adjacent selection-list behaviour, no AC
overlap with this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should priority ordering apply? (A) within each group only, (B) globally across the whole list, (C) both" — Answer (producer): **A — within each group only**. Source: interactive reply (intake round, recommended option accepted).
- Q2: "Stability definition — (A) content-deterministic grouping via canonical sort before fit, (B) keep packing, only stabilise within-group ordering" — Answer (producer): **A — content-deterministic grouping**. Source: interactive reply (recommended option accepted).
- Q3: "Scope of the change — (A) both mirrors kept in sync, (B) herdr only, (C) core only" — Answer (producer): **A — both, kept in sync**. Source: interactive reply (recommended option accepted). Research: confirmed the duplicate lives at `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B Q2c.

# Remove the heartbeat skill (superseded by the downtime dispatcher)

## Problem statement

The `heartbeat` skill (`/skill:heartbeat`) predates the herdr downtime dispatcher and duplicates — while contradicting — it. It is not in use: no invocation appears anywhere in the Pi session archive, and nothing in `wl`, the herdr plugin, cron, systemd or the test suite calls it. Keeping it costs two drifted copies of the same script that must both be maintained, plus a second, off-contract work-item ranking path.

## Evidence gathered (2026-10-30)

**No usage:**

- `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: zero occurrences of `/skill:heartbeat` as a user prompt (`"text":"/skill:heartbeat"` → 0 files); the ~1,000 hits are the skill-catalogue description embedded in every system prompt.
- No tool-result output of a real run (`"Flagged … for producer review"`, `"No items in completed/in_review queue"`) anywhere in the archive — those strings appear only inside the skill's own source/SKILL.md text.
- No crontab entry, no systemd timer, no herdr plugin hook, no caller in `packages/herdr/src` (the only "heartbeat" hits there are the unrelated *sync* heartbeat), no reference from any other skill.

**Superseded by the downtime dispatcher** (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`):

| | `heartbeat` skill | Downtime dispatcher |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | manual `/skill:heartbeat`, one action per call | continuous, leader-elected idle dispatch |
| Audit invocation | headless `pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>`, 600 s timeout, invisible | visible herdr pane, with pane monitor, stall resume and attempt budget |
| Audit threshold | review queue ≥ 10 (hard-coded) | review-queue gate `count >= browseItemCount` (live setting) + depth-aware audit batching |
| Candidate ranking | `wl next` — a **second ranking path** | "dispatcher == Herdr list head"; a second ranking is explicitly disallowed |
| `needsProducerReview` | set as a "look at this next" nudge on a sparse queue | a **dispatch hold**, set only on attempt-budget exhaustion |

**Duplicate drift:** `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` (resolved at runtime) and `skill/heartbeat/` (imported by the tests) are separate git-tracked copies that have diverged in their audit dispatch (`pi -p` vs `audit_runner.py`); the parity guard in `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py` exists only to stop further divergence. Removal eliminates the drift by construction.

**Deliberate coverage loss:** automated audit dispatch without herdr. The dispatcher lives in the herdr plugin and requires idle local-LLM capacity; a herdr-less mode would need a new implementation against the dispatcher's contract. Accepted — there is no herdr-less deployment today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/heartbeat/` and `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` are removed from the repository, so `/skill:heartbeat` no longer resolves in Pi and no duplicate copy remains.
2. `tests/skill/heartbeat/` (unit and integration suites) is removed; no test imports or references the heartbeat module.
3. The `README.md` feature blurb and the docs table row advertising the heartbeat skill are removed.
4. Stale prose is corrected: `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` no longer lists heartbeat as a `wl` consumer (inventory table and both summary rows), and `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` no longer refers to "heartbeat tooling" as a queue consumer.
5. The superseded work items recorded as deleted with the dispatcher named as the replacement: heartbeat audit notifications (WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI) and the `.pi` copy-drift item (WL-0MVVM0SLV0053QP8). *(Both were soft-deleted at filing time; this AC needs no implementation work — verify only that nothing still references them.)*
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (CHANGELOG.md is release-managed and excluded).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/heartbeat/` — delete (SKILL.md, `scripts/heartbeat.py`, `__init__.py`).
- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` — delete (runtime copy).
- `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py`, `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat_integration.py` — delete alongside the skill.
- `README.md` — remove the feature blurb (~line 11) and the docs table row (~line 140).
- `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — drop heartbeat from the `wl`-consumer inventory and per-invocation rows.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` — reword the "heartbeat/release tooling" reference (~line 74).
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — remove the heartbeat entry from the known skill-behaviour-drift note (~line 735) if it becomes stale.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the downtime dispatcher is the sole replacement for background audit dispatch; no herdr-less automation exists to preserve.
- **Assumption:** the "ready for producer review prior to a new release" report has no unique consumer (the ship/release gate and worklist header cover it); if that changes, it belongs in the worklist header, not a standalone skill.
- **Risk — muscle memory:** a user typing `/skill:heartbeat` will now get "skill not found" rather than a silent no-op. Accepted; the failure is loud and harmless.
- **Risk — stale references:** prose in `docs/dev/` and the README mentions the skill in several places; AC4 covers the substantive ones and a repo-wide grep for `heartbeat` (excluding the unrelated sync heartbeat and `CHANGELOG.md`) should come back clean.
- **Scope creep guard:** do not port heartbeat's sparse-queue nudge into the dispatcher — `wl reviewed <id> true` plus the TUI icon already cover manual producer flagging.

## Related work

- `Create a heartbeat skill for automated work item monitoring (WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD)` — the original item, now superseded.
- `Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless pi -p vs herdr pane (WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7)` — documents the headless-visibility gap that led here.
- `Herdr plugin: use notification system (toasts) instead of bottom-line status updates (WL-0MSACL482002RNYH)` — the toast plumbing the (withdrawn) notification proposal would have reused.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the replacement mechanism.

# Reduce per-command production startup cost (re-scoped from WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY — Investigate in-process CLI harness cost
**Decision source:** child 1 profile (WL-0MVVXFXM6007QZ2L, commit ebde3586) + child 3 decision gate (WL-0MVVXG4B200968BF).

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want a warm CLI invocation against an already-initialised store
to skip the per-call SQLite schema/migration bootstrap and YAML config re-parse,
so the ~2.2 ms (47 %) of every data-access call that is startup work stops being
paid again on each invocation — in the test suite's ~1200 in-process calls and in
real operator use.

## Context

Measured attribution (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` § 'In-process CLI harness
cost', `bench/inproc-harness-profile.json`), median of 5, fresh temp store:

| scenario | total | db open (schema+migrations) | config load | harness-side |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wl list --json` | 4.7 ms | 2.2 ms (47.3 %) | 0.0 ms | 1.5 ms (32.5 %) |
| `wl status` | 4.0 ms | 1.8 ms (44.8 %) | 0.2 ms (5.0 %) | 1.0 ms (25.4 %) |
| `wl create` | 5.1 ms | 2.1 ms (42.1 %) | 0.2 ms (3.8 %) | 0.8 ms (16.2 %) |

`getDatabase()` (`src/cli-utils.ts`) calls `loadConfigRelaxed()` — which reads and
`yaml.load`s the config files — and then constructs `WorklogDatabase`
(`src/database.ts` → `packages/shared/src/database.ts`), which builds a
`SqlitePersistentStore` and runs the schema/migration bootstrap on every open.
This is production behaviour (not a test-harness artefact), so the fix belongs in
`src/`/`packages/shared` rather than in `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opening an already-migrated store at the current schema version does **not**
  re-run the full migration scan on every open: the fast path is detected by a
  cheap schema-version comparison (e.g. `PRAGMA user_version` / a version table),
  and the slow path is still taken for a new, older, or partially-migrated store.
- Config load is not repeated needlessly within one process when the config files
  have not changed (cache keyed on the resolved config file paths plus their
  mtime/size or content hash), and the cache is invalidated when a file changes.
- Behaviour is unchanged: the full test suite passes with the same test counts,
  and schema-creation/migration/integrity tests are green (including downgrade
  and partial-migration cases).
- Median `wl list --json` warm per-call cost against a fresh temp store drops by
  **>= 30 %** versus the child 1 baseline (4.7 ms → <= 3.3 ms), measured on the
  same host as the median of >= 5 runs with load average quoted, using
  `npm run benchmark:inproc-harness -- --runs 5` (a bench script, never an
  ad-hoc vitest invocation).
- `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` (WL-0MVVXG3UW00250V5) is regenerated for the
  improved numbers and its guard test still passes; the before/after medians and
  the host load are recorded on this item.
- No test-harness workaround is introduced: `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` keeps
  constructing a database per call, so the saving is real production saving.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — store open + schema/migration bootstrap.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase` construction/open path.
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `getDatabase` (calls `loadConfigRelaxed` per call).
- `src/config.ts` — `loadConfig` / `loadConfigRelaxed` YAML parse.
- `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts`, `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` — measurement.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — record the before/after numbers.

## Notes

- The migration path must stay obviously correct: a missed migration is data
  corruption, so the fast path must be conservatively gated and covered by tests
  that start from a real older schema.
- Any per-process config cache must be invalidated on file change; tests must
  exercise that invalidation (edit the config between two calls in one process).
data.title: Reduce per-command production startup: skip repeated schema/migration bootstrap and config re-parse

# Remove the `do-not-delegate` flag from the worklog system

## Problem statement

The worklog system currently carries a dedicated `do-not-delegate` tag and a first-class `--do-not-delegate` CLI flag, plus a `--force` override on `wl github delegate`. That mechanism predates the use of the `assignee` field as the scheduling-hold signal: a **non-empty `assignee` now means "held / not available for delegation"**, and an empty `assignee` means the item may be delegated. Keeping both mechanisms means two sources of truth for the same decision, duplicated documentation, a stale TUI/CLI surface, and a tag that every project's automation must special-case.

This item removes the redundant `do-not-delegate` flag and tag guard rail and makes the `assignee` field the single source of truth for delegate eligibility.

## Users

- **Automated dispatchers / schedulers** (for example the herdr downtime worker):
  *As a dispatcher, I want one unambiguous hold signal (`assignee`) so I never have to know whether an item is held by a tag, an assignee, or both, and my selection logic matches the delegate command's logic.*
- **Operators:**
  *As an operator, I want to set or release a delegation hold with the `assignee` field I already use for claims, instead of remembering a second, legacy flag.*
- **Maintainers:**
  *As a maintainer, I want the dead flag, its guard rail, its `--force` escape hatch, its tests and its documentation removed together, so no half-removed surface remains.*

## Rationale (why removal, not deprecation)

- `assignee` already expresses exactly the same intent: `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` and `fetcher.ts` document "a non-empty value is the scheduling hold" and clear it with `--assignee ""` (CAS-guarded with `--if-assignee`).
- The `do-not-delegate` tag is currently duplicated across the tag vocabulary and CLI flags, and must be replicated in every orchestrator (`implement.py`, helper scripts, herdr) to avoid livelocks.
- A tag can be added or removed independently of the claim/hold state, so it can drift out of sync with the assignee. One field cannot drift from itself.

## Desired behaviour

Delegation eligibility is determined solely by `assignee`:

- An item with a **non-empty `assignee`** is **held** and must not be delegated automatically (the delegate command refuses, with a clear message naming the holder).
- An item with an **empty/absent `assignee`** is eligible for delegation.
- Successful delegation continues to set `assignee` to `@github-copilot` (the existing post-assignment state), which naturally holds the item afterwards.
- The `do-not-delegate` tag is no longer written, read, documented or accepted as a CLI option. Any pre-existing `do-not-delegate` tags in stores become inert data and are not migrated automatically (see constraints).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — CLI surface removed.** `wl update` no longer accepts `--do-not-delegate` (option registration, argument normalisation list, and per-id tag mutation removed from `src/commands/update.ts`); `src/cli-types.ts` no longer declares `doNotDelegate`. Invoking the old flag fails as an unknown option rather than silently mutating tags.
- [ ] **AC2 — Delegate guard rail replaced.** `src/delegate-helper.ts` no longer inspects `item.tags` for `do-not-delegate`. Instead it refuses delegation when `item.assignee` is a non-empty string, returning a distinct error key (e.g. `held-by-assignee` / `assigned`) and a human-readable message that names the current assignee and explains that a non-empty assignee is the scheduling hold. `DelegateOptions.force` and the associated force-override warning are removed; the step-by-step docstring is updated.
- [ ] **AC3 — `--force` removed from `wl github delegate`.** `src/commands/github.ts` drops the `--force` option, stops passing `force` to `delegateWorkItem`, and maps the new held-by-assignee error to a clear CLI error (no `--force` hint). The existing interactive open-children confirmation is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC4 — Empty/absent assignee remains delegate-eligible.** Delegation still succeeds for an item with `assignee` unset or `""`, preserving the current happy path and the `assignee: '@github-copilot'` update after a successful assignment.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests updated.** Delete `tests/cli/update-do-not-delegate.test.ts`; remove the `do-not-delegate` cases from `tests/cli/update-batch.test.ts`; rewrite the `do-not-delegate` cases in `tests/cli/delegate-guard-rails.test.ts` as assignee-hold cases (held item refuses, empty/unset assignee proceeds, message names the holder); remove the `doNotDelegate` fake-CLI handling and `Boolean(item.doNotDelegate ?? false)` field from `tests/test-utils.ts`; update the test index in `tests/README.md`. Add/extend a regression test proving the tag is inert (an item still carrying `do-not-delegate` but with an empty assignee delegates normally).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated.** Remove the `--do-not-delegate` update examples/description and the `--force` delegate option from `CLI.md`; replace them with assignee-based guidance ("set `--assignee <holder>` to hold; clear with `--assignee ""` to release"). Update any delegate documentation that mentions the tag. No remaining user-facing reference to `do-not-delegate` in `CLI.md`, `README.md`, `tests/README.md`, or command help text.
- [ ] **AC7 — No behavioural regression elsewhere.** `assignee` CAS/claim semantics (`--if-assignee`, `--assignee ""`), successful-delegation state, and all other delegate guard rails (open-child warning, push/assign failure handling) are unchanged. Existing suite remains green.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes** and `npm run build` (or the project's documented build) succeeds.

## Constraints

- **Single source of truth.** Do not introduce a replacement tag or a migration that rewrites existing `do-not-delegate` tags into assignees automatically; per-project data migration, if desired, is a separate operator action.
- **Assignees set by other agents are holds.** Do not attempt to distinguish "producer hold" from "agent claim" in the delegate guard: any non-empty assignee means held.
- **No widening to herdr/implement.py.** This item removes the flag from the worklog system (CLI, helper, docs, tests). Updates to any consumer (`implement.py`, herdr, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`) that special-cases the tag are follow-ups and should be recorded, not folded in, unless they are required to keep the build green.
- **Backward compatibility:** removing a CLI option is an intentional breaking change. Call it out in the changelog/release note.
- **Preserve the open-children warning** and all non-`do-not-delegate` delegate behaviour exactly.

## Key files (verified in this checkout)

- `src/cli-types.ts` — `doNotDelegate?: string` declaration (~lines 109-110).
- `src/delegate-helper.ts` — `DelegateOptions.force` (~line 33), flow docstring (step 2, ~line 77), guard-rail block (~lines 114-127).
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--do-not-delegate` option (~line 49), normalisation lists (~lines 58, 65), parsing (~lines 212-219), per-id tag mutation (~lines 482-499).
- `src/commands/github.ts` — delegate `--force` option (~line 767), `force` passthrough (~line 825), error mapping (~lines 847-855).
- `tests/cli/update-do-not-delegate.test.ts` — delete.
- `tests/cli/update-batch.test.ts` — cases ~lines 470-500.
- `tests/cli/delegate-guard-rails.test.ts` — header comment and cases ~lines 276-290.
- `tests/test-utils.ts` — `doNotDelegate` field (~line 241) and fake-CLI reference (~line 407).
- `tests/README.md` — entries at lines 92 and 120.
- `CLI.md` — lines 286, 321-325, 1197.
- Generated `dist/` and `package/dist/` outputs — regenerated by the build, not hand-edited.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a non-empty `assignee` is already the intended delegation-hold signal in every consumer; confirmed in `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` (~lines 193-209) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (~lines 305-309).
- **Risk (silent eligibility):** items currently protected only by a `do-not-delegate` tag will become delegate-eligible if their assignee is empty. Mitigation: the replacement guard is tested, and the removal is documented in the changelog as a breaking change so operators can audit tagged items first.
- **Risk (automation drift):** an external orchestrator may still pass `--do-not-delegate`; removing the option makes that fail loudly (which is the desired signal) rather than silently ignoring the hold.
- **Risk (partial removal):** generated `dist/` artifacts could keep exposing the old flag if the build is skipped; AC8 requires a build and AC1/AC3 verify the CLI surface.
- **No schema change:** `do-not-delegate` lives only in the free-form `tags` array; there is no DB column or migration to remove.

## Related / follow-up work

- Consumer cleanup (record as follow-ups if needed): `implement.py`'s `do-not-delegate` selection guard and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` references, once they exist on `dev`.
- Store hygiene: an operator may optionally strip the now-inert tag from existing items (`wl update <id> --tags ...`), but that is not part of this item.

## Appendix: verification performed while writing this item

- `grep -rn "do-not-delegate\|doNotDelegate" src/ tests/ --include="*.ts"` → `src/cli-types.ts`, `src/delegate-helper.ts`, `src/commands/update.ts`, `src/commands/github.ts`, and the three test files plus `tests/test-utils.ts`.
- `grep -rn "do-not-delegate" --include="*.md"` (excluding `node_modules`/`dist`) → `CLI.md`, `tests/README.md`.
- `packages/tui` and `packages/herdr` contain no `do-not-delegate`/`doNotDelegate` implementation (the README line about a TUI `g` delegate shortcut is stale; no TUI delegate code references the tag).
- `delegateWorkItem` sets `assignee: '@github-copilot'` on success, confirming assignee is the post-delegation hold.
data.title: Remove the do-not-delegate flag from the worklog system

# Fixed 900 ms registration window causes load-induced flake

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVHVZTYA003TNN0 (test-suite parallelism: maxWorkers 4 -> 6)

## Problem

`tests/cli/process-lifecycle.test.ts` > *"killTrackedProcesses is registered for
process exit so no orphans remain after test worker dies"* spawns
`sleep 0.3 && sleep 30` through the in-process harness (`execAsync`) and then
waits a fixed `setTimeout(r, 900)` before asserting
`pidTrackingSet.size > 0`.

That 900 ms window is a timing assumption, not an assertion about behaviour.
When two canonical full suites ran concurrently on the shared 16-core host
(12 heavy forks), the spawn had not registered within 900 ms and the test
failed with `expected 0 to be greater than 0`. It passed in every serial run
before and after, so this is a load-induced flake, not a product regression.

Observed evidence (2026-11-02, WL-0MVHVZTYA003TNN0 re-validation):
- Concurrent pair: 1 failure — `process-lifecycle.test.ts:256`
  (`AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0`).
- 3 serial runs of the same tree: all green.

## Proposed change

Replace the fixed 900 ms sleep with a bounded poll (e.g. wait until
`pidTrackingSet.size > 0` or a generous timeout, polling every 25-50 ms), so
the assertion tests the registration behaviour with a real bound instead of a
fixed scheduling guess. Keep the same asserted outcome (tracked process
present, then killed by `killTrackedProcesses`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test waits for `pidTrackingSet.size > 0` with a bounded poll (no fixed
  single sleep as the only synchronisation) and still fails on a real
  regression (e.g. `killTrackedProcesses()` no longer clearing the set).
- The test is green in 3 consecutive serial canonical runs, and green in a
  deliberately contended pair of concurrent full-suite runs at
  `maxWorkers: 6` (the regime that surfaced the flake).
- No change to product code — test robustness only.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRTSOTF1002I8WZ** – CLI and exec auto-registration of spawned processes (completed)
- **WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY** – Documentation for process lifecycle management (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5ICN0098ID6** – Remove unused WorkItem import from index.ts (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — matched: 0mvhvztya003tnn0, acceptance, asserted, assertion, behaviour (+89 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: asserted, assertion, assumption, behaviour, bound (+82 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, behaviour, bound, bounded, canonical (+78 more)

## Summary

WL-0MVK01BBD005V7KK added a pure-fallback content fingerprint to the two CLI audit-write commands named in its scope (`wl audit-set` and `wl update --audit-text`). Two other synthetic audit-write surfaces still resolve `fingerprint = null`:

Neither was in this item's declared scope ("Manual (synthetic) audit writes are the CLI surface: src/commands/audit-result.ts and src/commands/update.ts"), so it was recorded rather than widened.

Apply the same fallback: `computeContentFingerprint({ title, description })` from `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`, after the existing explicit/embedded resolution. For `create` the fingerprint must be computed after the item is created (or from the input title/description, which are the same values written).

# Document the link-farm setup that has now shipped (parent AC1b)

## Goal

As an agent whose change touches `packages/shared/src/**`, I want the supported,
tested way to make my change visible to my worktree's own build/test gate
documented in one place, so I get a truthful green/red instead of the main
checkout's stale `dist`.

## Hold cleared — dispatchable (mechanism has landed)

This child covers parent AC1(b). It was created held (`needsProducerReview`)
because the link-farm mechanism it documents did not exist at planning time.

**The producer cleared the hold on 2026-11-05** (answer A to the parent's
Appendix question), because the mechanism has shipped:
`SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` (SorraAgents) is `completed` / `in_review`. This item has
no assignee and `needsProducerReview` is false — it is startable.

**Status at re-plan (2026-11-05):** the mechanism shipped in
`SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` (SorraAgents, now `completed` / `in_review`).
`implement.py start` materialises a worktree-local `node_modules` **link farm**
(`_materialise_link_farm` / `_reconcile_link_farm`), overrides every workspace
package consumed by path (`@worklog/shared` → the worktree's own
`packages/shared`), and reports the result in its `start` JSON as
`shared_resolution` / `shared_resolution_ok`.

Nothing else blocks: the page to edit exists, the sibling module-resolution
section landed (`905b46e1`), and the doc-link check that guards the new links
landed (`a58a5818`). (The hold existed because cross-store dependency edges
cannot be expressed — WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD.)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Farm documented as built (AC1b).** The page describes the layout
   `implement.py start` actually creates — verified against the shipped
   `implement.py`, not from memory of the plan: a real
   `<worktree>/node_modules` directory of one symlink per main-checkout entry
   (`.bin` linked as a whole directory), a real directory per scope (`@types`,
   `@worklog`, …) holding one symlink per scoped package, and — for every
   workspace package the main checkout consumes by path — a link to the
   **worktree's own** package directory. It also states the degradation: a repo
   with no path-consumed workspace package keeps the previous whole-directory
   `node_modules` symlink.
2. **Refresh path documented.** The sanctioned refresh is named as the shipped
   command (`implement.py start <work-item-id>` — reconciliation is
   idempotent; there is no separate refresh subcommand), stated as the only
   sanctioned alternative to `npm install` in a worktree, and noted as the fix
   when the main checkout's dependency set changes.
3. **Verification pointer documented and proven.** The page names how a reader
   confirms the farm from inside a worktree: `implement.py start`'s
   `shared_resolution_ok` / `shared_resolution` report block plus the
   `readlink -f node_modules/@worklog/shared` check, expecting
   `<worktree>/packages/shared` (not the main checkout). The same evidence is
   recorded on this item: a fresh `implement.py start` worktree resolves
   `@worklog/shared` to `<worktree>/packages/shared`, and a probe edit under
   `packages/shared/src/**` is observed by
   `run_tests.py --type full --scope full` (green) — the fact this item exists
   to establish that the pre-farm symlink-only setup could not deliver.
4. **Stale claims corrected (AC1c after the fix).** The page no longer tells
   readers that no link farm exists or that a `packages/shared` edit is only
   testable by importing source by relative path. The stale-`dist` signature
   section states that, post-farm, "worktree shared edits invisible to the gate"
   means a **broken or stale farm**, and names the refresh step as the fix.
   The same pre-fix claim in
   `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` (its subtitle and
   its "implement.py auto-symlink" fix description) is corrected, with a
   one-line note that the symlink was superseded by the farm.
5. **Links and gates.** New relative links pass `tests/docs/dev-link-check.test.ts`

# Goal

As an agent or operator performing worklog housekeeping, I want `wl delete` to accept
`--deleted-by` and `--delete-reason`, so that a soft-delete records *why* the item was removed in the
same command that removes it — instead of requiring a second `wl update` correction pass that is easy
to forget.

Discovered during: WL-0MVYEQKAM003THSP housekeeping (2026-11-02) — the machine-specific epic sweep
needed a non-default reason, and the CLI could not express it.

# Problem

`wl delete` hardcodes both attribution values:

```ts
// src/commands/delete.ts:81-82
const deletedBy = await getConfiguredUserEmail();
const deleteReason = 'deleted via wl delete';
```

`deleteReason` is therefore **not expressible from the CLI at all** — every CLI soft-delete claims
"deleted via wl delete" regardless of intent. `deletedBy` is only ever the configured git identity.

Three concrete consequences:

1. **Intent is lost.** A housekeeping sweep (duplicate, superseded, machine-specific, wrong project)
   is indistinguishable after the fact from an accidental delete. `deleteReason` is persisted on the
   item, synced, and is the field a post-mortem reads — so the loss is permanent and shared with every
   collaborator.
2. **The workaround is two commands and silently skippable.** The only way to set a real reason today
   is `wl delete <id>` followed by `wl update <id> --delete-reason "..."`. That second step is legal
   because the soft-delete guard (`src/commands/update.ts`) permits changes to `deletedBy` /
   `deleteReason` on an already-deleted item — but it is undiscoverable, and skipping it leaves the
   wrong reason recorded with no error.
3. **CLI/API divergence.** The REST API already supports exactly this —
   `src/api.ts` reads `deletedBy` and `deleteReason` from query parameters, defaulting to
   `'deleted via API'` (added by WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO F4). The CLI, which is the primary interface for
   agents, lacks the equivalent.

Attribution is also load-bearing for replication, not just for humans: per the delete command's own
comment, the merge layer's delete-side protection **only propagates attributed deletes** over a live
remote item — an unattributed delete silently fails to propagate. So the flags must never be able to
produce a blank `deletedBy` by accident.

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — Both flags record verbatim.** `wl delete <id> --deleted-by "agent-x" --delete-reason "duplicate of WL-XXXX"`
      persists exactly those values on the item (verified via `--json` output and a subsequent
      `wl show <id> --json`).
- [ ] **AC-2 — Recursive delete propagates attribution.** With `--deleted-by`/`--delete-reason` and a
      parent that has descendants, the target **and every descendant** carry the supplied values (a
      descendant asserting the legacy default instead is a failure).
- [ ] **AC-3 — Defaults unchanged when the flags are omitted.** Omitting both preserves today's
      behaviour exactly: `deleteReason` = `deleted via wl delete`, `deletedBy` = configured git
      identity. Pinned by a test so existing callers (and their assertions) cannot regress.
- [ ] **AC-4 — Attribution can never be silently lost.** An empty or whitespace-only `--deleted-by`
      must either fall back to the configured git identity or fail with a clear, non-zero-exit error
      naming the problem — it must **not** write a blank `deletedBy`, which would produce a delete that
      cannot propagate through merge. Pinned by a test for both `--deleted-by ""` and `--deleted-by "   "`.
- [ ] **AC-5 — No breaking change to the JSON/batch contract.** The per-id `results` array, the
      `deleted`/`failed` summary, the legacy single-id fields and the skip semantics for duplicate or
      descendant ids are unchanged; the flags are purely additive. Existing delete suites
      (`tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts`, `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts`) pass unmodified.
- [ ] **AC-6 — Surface and docs updated.** `wl delete --help` documents both flags (including the
      default values and the AC-4 fallback); `DeleteOptions` in `src/cli-types.ts` gains both optional
      fields; the soft-delete section of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (which states `deletedBy` is
      "set by `wl delete`") notes that the CLI can now set attribution explicitly, matching the REST
      API.

# Key Files

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — the hardcoded `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` at lines 81-82; the `.option()` declarations; the JSON `results` builder.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — `DeleteOptions` (line ~201): add `deletedBy?: string` and `deleteReason?: string`.
- `tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts` — the natural home for AC-1/2/3/5 coverage (in-process CLI harness, real DB mutations).
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` — ensure the new flags do not affect the auto-sync invocation contract.
- `src/api.ts` — REST parity reference (lines ~208 and ~430) for naming, defaults and the `|| fallback` shape to mirror.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — the soft-delete guard that currently makes the two-step workaround legal; its comments document the attribution/merge rule behind AC-4.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — soft-delete exclusion section (~line 2305) referencing `deletedBy` set by `wl delete`.

# Non-goals

- Changing `wl delete`'s recursion, sync, batch or skip semantics.
- Adding a prompt/interactive confirmation for the reason — flags only.
- Changing the REST API's existing `deleted via API` default.
- Retrofitting reasons onto already-deleted items (a separate, opt-in cleanup if ever wanted).

# Notes

- Suggested defaults: `--delete-reason` default stays `deleted via wl delete`; `--deleted-by` default
  stays the configured git identity, with the supplied value taking precedence (`options.deletedBy || await getConfiguredUserEmail() || ''`),
  mirroring `src/api.ts`.
- Alternatively `--deleted-by` could be *rejected* when blank rather than falling back; either satisfies
  AC-4, but the fall-back variant matches the API and is less disruptive to scripts that pass an empty
  variable.
data.title: wl delete: add --deleted-by and --delete-reason flags (CLI parity with REST API attribution)

# Manually created tabs go to the left, dispatched tabs to the right

## Problem statement

Tabs spawned by the operator from the Herdr Worklog selection list (e.g. `p` for plan, `i` for implement, `p-n` for a new pi session, or any other ID-carrying interactive dispatch) currently append at the **right** end of the workspace tab row, away from the Worklog (extensions/plugin) tab they belong next to. Automated dispatch tabs (downtime dispatcher) append there too. Operator-created tabs should instead land immediately to the **left** of the Worklog/extensions tab, while automated dispatches keep today's right-side placement.

## Users

- The operator (producer/developer) driving work out of the Herdr Worklog selection list. Example user stories:
  - "As an operator, when I hit `i` to implement a work item, I want the new item tab to appear next to the Worklog tab so my manually opened sessions stay grouped and my work-in-progress tabs don't get pushed out of view at the far right of the tab row."
  - "As an operator, when I open a new pi session from the selection list, I want it beside the other manually opened sessions rather than at the end of a long tab row."

## Acceptance Criteria

- An interactive dispatch that **creates a new tab** (ID-carrying commands such as `/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, prompt/`!!`/`!` commands carrying a work-item ID, and a new-pi-session dispatch from the selection list) places that tab immediately to the **left of the Worklog (extensions/plugin) tab** in the invoking workspace.
- Automated dispatches (downtime dispatcher) place their tabs at the default right-side position exactly as today — no behaviour change.
- Tab repositioning is implemented via the herdr socket API `tab.move` with `insert_index` set to the extensions tab's index (or an equivalent herdr CLI/socket mechanism available at implement time); the tab is first created as today and then moved.
- Fail-open: when the Worklog/extensions tab cannot be resolved (no plugin pane, no tab labelled `Worklog`, multiple/ambiguous matches) or `tab.move` fails, the newly created tab stays at its default right-side position — the dispatch is never blocked, dropped, or placed in a wrong workspace.
- Reuse semantics are preserved: an **existing** item-ID tab is adopted without being moved (only freshly provisioned tabs are repositioned; a reused tab's position is the operator's own arrangement).
- At least one automated test (unit or integration) covers each of: left placement for an interactively created tab, default right placement for a dispatcher-created tab, and fail-open when the extensions tab or the move is unavailable.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No herdr core changes in scope: herdr 0.9.5 CLI `tab create` has no insert/position flag — the repositioning must go through the socket API (`tab.move` with `insert_index`) or an existing CLI mechanism, and must tolerate the capability being absent (fail-open).
- The "extensions tab" is the tab hosting the Worklog selection list / plugin TUI — i.e. the tab containing a pane labelled `Work Items` (`PLUGIN_PANE_LABEL`), commonly renamed to `Worklog` by `open-worklog-tab.sh`.
- Interactive and dispatcher callers share the same tab-creation choke points (`createTabInWorkspace`, the anchor resolvers); the change must distinguish the two so only operator-initiated creation repositions.
- Root-pane cleanup semantics (fail-safe liveness check, WS-holder placeholder close) and the fail-open dispatch guarantees from the interactive item-tab work must be preserved.
- Keep changes surgical; do not introduce a second tab mechanism or restructure the dispatcher-adoption logic.

## Existing state

- `herdr tab create` appends a new tab at the right end of the workspace tab row; both the interactive item-ID path and the downtime dispatcher path create tabs this way, so all tabs land to the right of existing tabs.
- Interactive ID-carrying dispatches provision a tab labelled exactly `<itemId>` via `getItemTabAnchor` (`dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`) — created on first use, adopted thereafter — split via `send-to-pi.sh`/`run-in-pane.sh` with `--anchor`, with fail-safe placeholder root-pane cleanup.
- The downtime dispatcher provisions its own tabs (Dispatcher workspace / project workspace item tabs) through the same herdr CLI tab primitives.
- herdr socket API exposes `tab.move` (with `insert_index`) and emits `tab.moved` events carrying the requested `insert_index` and the updated ordered tab list.

## Desired change

- At the tab-creation choke point, add an interactive-placement mode (e.g. a `placement: 'left-of-extensions'` flag/param, defaulting to today's behaviour) set only by the interactive dispatch path.
- After a freshly provisioned tab is created for an interactive dispatch, resolve the Worklog/extensions tab in that workspace (pane labelled `Work Items`, falling back to a tab labelled `Worklog`) and `tab.move` the new tab to `insert_index` = that tab's index (immediately left of it). Fail-open at every boundary.
- Dispatcher-created tabs, and adopted (reused) interactive tabs, are untouched.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` — `createTabInWorkspace` (and any new `tab move` CLI/socket helper) — the tab-creation choke point.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor` provisioning path (interactive item-ID tabs).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` / `closeInteractiveTabRootPane` (interactive vs dispatcher call-site split).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` / `downtime-worker.pane.ts` — dispatcher tab provisioning (must remain right-placed).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` — `PLUGIN_PANE_LABEL` (`Work Items`) and any new placement-mode types/labels.
- Tests alongside each module (`*.test.ts`) plus the split-guard baselines if CLI helper signatures change.

## Related work

- WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — "Implement: interactive item-tab placement" (completed) — established the interactive item-ID tab anchor + `--anchor` forwarding this work extends.
- WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS — "Pi processes should start in a work item tab" (completed epic) — parent of the interactive placement work.
- WL-0MUYI3K8H007MPKF / WL-0MUYI3JRC006115V — interactive item-tab root-pane cleanup (implement/test).
- WL-0MUYI3KPB0024U86 — "Docs: interactive item-ID-tab placement" (completed) — docs companion to update.
- WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG — "Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace…" (completed) — dispatcher anchor-by-ID workspace; the automated path that stays right-placed.
- WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU — "dispatcher workspace has useless pane" (completed) — root-pane cleanup precedent.
- WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ (refactor) — decomposed `dispatcher-anchor.ts`; placement code now lives in the split modules above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Extensions-tab resolution ambiguity** — if multiple tabs contain a `Work Items`-labelled pane, or both a `Worklog`-labelled tab and a `Work Items` pane tab exist, the anchor choice must be deterministic; fail-open (leave tab right) on none/ambiguous rather than misplace.
- **herdr `tab.move` availability** — depends on the socket API of the running herdr (0.9.5 supports it); if absent or failing, the tab stays where created (right) — never block the dispatch.
- **Created-vs-reused signal** — repositioning must apply only to freshly provisioned tabs; reusing the existing `onCreate` create-vs-reuse observer avoids disturbing tabs the operator arranged manually.
- **Scope-creep risk** — reordering existing/adopted tabs, changing dispatcher (right) placement, or reworking the pane-splitting (non-tab) interactive paths are out of scope; record any such follow-up as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption: keybinding coverage** — `p`/`i`/`p-n` and other interactive dispatches resolve to the interactive `onCommand` path (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`); treat any interactive dispatch that creates a tab as operator-created. Non-tab (current-pane split) routes are unaffected.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What is 'the extensions tab'?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "(a) The tab hosting the Worklog selection list / plugin TUI (currently renamed 'Worklog')." Source: interactive reply, this intake session (WL-0MVZ88G51004IYHW).
- Q2: "Acceptable implementation mechanism (herdr 0.9.5 CLI `tab create` has no insert flag)?" — Answer (operator): "(a) create the tab as today, then reposition via herdr socket API `tab.move` with `insert_index` = index of the extensions tab." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Which interactions count as operator-created, and where should the change live?" — Answer (operator): "(a) All interactive dispatch paths — item-ID tabs from `p`/`i`/other ID-carrying commands AND `p-n` new-pi-session tabs — moved left, applied in `packages/herdr` tab-creation code (`createTabInWorkspace`/anchor resolvers)." Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKVZ3RBL10DFPPW** – Use Alt+Right Arrow to advance focus (replace Tab) (completed)
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC** – Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace (route each prefix to its own tab) (completed)
- **WL-0MSKUAT5D00443GA** – Impl: tab-focus-gated visibility in visibility.ts + docs (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: automated, created, dispatcher, downtime, extensions, herdr, implement, left, list, manually, need, new, now, operator, place, plan, processes, right, selection, session, spawning, tab, tabs, they, when
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: automated, created, dispatcher, downtime, extensions, herdr, implement, left, list, manually, need, new, now, operator, place, plan, processes, right, selection, session, spawning, tab, tabs, they, when
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: automated, dispatcher, downtime, extensions, herdr, implement, left, list, need, new, now, operator, place, plan, processes, right, selection, session, spawning, tab, tabs, they, when

# Fetcher split guard: freeze surface, ceiling and dependency direction

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)
**Source:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` = 2,365 lines, 47 exports, 13 sections (dev @ 4e69171d)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `fetcher.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1–AC4 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an unchanged
public surface at `./fetcher.js`, unmodified test files, and no new circular
imports. Nothing in the repo enforces these for `fetcher.ts` today.

The `downtime-worker`, `worklist` and `index` decompositions already built this
machinery: `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` exports the generic
predicates (`loadModuleIndex`, `consumerImportNames`, `findMissingExports`,
`resolveImportTarget`, `isTypeOnlyImport`, `findCycleBaselineViolations`,
`findOversizedModules`, `findAllowlistViolations`, …) and each family adds a
thin `<family>-family.ts` config module. **Reuse `scan.ts` unchanged; never edit
it** — this child adds only the fetcher-specific gaps.

Facts captured at plan time (dev @ 4e69171d, `packages/herdr`):

- **2,365 lines**, 47 exports, 13 logical sections.
- **68 consumer files** import from `./fetcher.js`: 16 production
  (`index.ts`, `hydrator.ts`, `worklist.ts`, `smart-selection.ts`,
  `index.claim.ts`, `index.downtime-resolvers.ts`, `worklist.detail.ts`,
  `worklist.state.ts`, `dispatch-view.ts`, `visibility.ts`, `code-freeze.ts`,
  `agent-tracker.ts`, `index.interactive.ts`, `index.settings.ts`,
  `md-note-edit.ts`, `worklist.meta.ts`) + 52 test files.
- **42 distinct symbols** are imported by consumers — the frozen surface:
  `BlockerRef`, `DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP`, `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `WorkItem`,
  `_resetWlSpawnStats`, `_wlSpawnStats`, `buildWlArgs`, `buildWlArgsForRoot`,
  `checkWlAvailable`, `claimWorkItem`, `clearFetchMemo`,
  `createInProcessRefreshScope`, `extractItems`, `extractJson`,
  `fetchActionableCount`, `fetchBlockersForItem`, `fetchChildrenForItem`,
  `fetchChildrenForItems`, `fetchCompletedItemCount`, `fetchItemDetails`,
  `fetchItemsByPriority`, `fetchItemsByStage`, `fetchNextItems`,
  `fetchOutboundDepsForItems`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, `getExecFileAsync`,
  `getInProcessOpenStats`, `getWlSpawnCap`, `getWorklogDir`,
  `markNeedsProducerReviewWorkItem`, `resetExecFileAsync`,
  `resetInProcessOpenStats`, `resetWlSpawnCap`, `resetWorklogDir`,
  `rollbackClaimWorkItem`, `runWlSync`, `setExecFileAsync`, `setWlSpawnCap`,
  `setWorklogDir`, `ReviewQueueState`.
- The live import graph already contains pre-existing cycles; the gate forbids a
  **new** cycle member or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Scope

- New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts`
  (vitest).
- New `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/fetcher-family.ts` — config, scanners
  and baseline producer for the fetcher family (mirrors `index-family.ts`).
- New committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-baseline.json` —
  the 42 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
  source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
- **No production code moves. No existing test file is modified.**

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` exists and passes on the
   current (unsplit) tree **before any production code moves**; no existing test
   file is modified (parent AC3).
2. `fetcher.split-baseline.json` records the 42 consumer-imported symbol names
   with provenance, and is reproducible via
   `npx tsx packages/herdr/test/split-guard/fetcher-family.ts --write-baseline`
   (command recorded in the file and in the module doc comment).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported from
   `./fetcher.js` with its recorded kind (`value`/`type`); a removed or renamed
   symbol fails the test with the symbol name in the message.
4. **Size gate:** every `packages/herdr/src/fetcher*.ts` production module is
   ≤1,000 lines. The allowlist starts as `["fetcher.ts"]` (the pre-split
   monolith) and the test asserts the allowlist can only shrink — the final
   child empties it.
5. **Cycle gate:** the pre-existing cross-module cycle baseline is recorded in
   `fetcher-family.ts`; the gate fails on a new cycle member or a new
   **runtime** (non-type-only) cycle edge.
6. **Barrel-value-import gate:** no extracted `fetcher.*.ts` module may import
   the `./fetcher.js` barrel at runtime (type-only imports are allowed).
7. The guard suite runs green against the unsplit tree and is recorded as the
   evidence comment on this item.

## Minimal implementation

1. Create `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/fetcher-family.ts`, importing the
   generic predicates from `./scan.ts` (never editing `scan.ts`); add only the
   fetcher-specific consumer discovery (static `./fetcher.js` imports across
   `src/**/*.ts`) and the baseline producer.
2. Generate and commit `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-baseline.json`.
3. Write `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` with the four gates
   (surface, size, cycle, barrel-value-import) and the allowlist-shrink
   assertion.
4. Run the guard suite via `/skill:test` (changed scope) and record the output
   in a comment on this item.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/fetcher-family.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — read-only (reused, never edited)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — read-only (must not change)

## Dependencies

Blocks: every extraction child (2–7) and the close-out child (8).

## Notes

This child is the only one permitted to introduce the guard machinery. The
allowlist starts non-empty (the monolith itself) and only the final child may
empty it.

# Extract fetcher types and arg/exec primitives

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
**Source ranges (dev @ 4e69171d, 2,365 lines):** types 28–37, 277–375, 631–642, 760–785, 1073–1088, 1193–1209, 1717–1756, 1905–1945, 2142–2157 · `formatWlError` 37–66 · worklog-dir + wl-arg + exec seam 66–151
**New modules:** `fetcher.types.ts` (~250 lines), `fetcher.args.ts` (~140 lines)

## Goal

As a fetcher maintainer, I want the pure data types and the worklog-dir /
`wl`-argument / exec-seam primitives in dedicated leaf modules, so that changing
a type or the CLI invocation shape no longer means scrolling through 2,365 lines
of runtime logic.

## Scope (move-only)

Move **verbatim** (with provenance comments and section banners):

- **`fetcher.types.ts`:** `WlError`, `WorkItem`, `BlockerRef`,
  `DependencyTargetRef`, `ReviewQueueState`, `InProcessOpenStats`,
  `InProcessRefreshScope`, `WorklistBundle`, `RootSubstitution`,
  `ClaimResult`, and the internal `InProcessDb`/`InProcessDbCtor` type
  declarations.
- **`fetcher.args.ts`:** `formatWlError`, `setWorklogDir`, `getWorklogDir`,
  `buildWlArgs`, `buildWlArgsForRoot`, `resetWorklogDir`, `setExecFileAsync`,
  `getExecFileAsync`, `resetExecFileAsync`.

Do **not** move behaviour, rename a symbol, re-order a union/`Record` member, or
drop a doc comment. Leave every runtime fetch function for its own child.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `fetcher.types.ts` and `fetcher.args.ts` exist and each is ≤1,000 lines
   (`wc -l`); the split-guard size gate passes with the allowlist unchanged
   (still only `fetcher.ts`).
2. Every moved symbol keeps its exact name, exported kind
   (`const`/`type`/`interface`/`function`), signature and value; the barrel
   re-exports each of the 42 consumer-imported symbols it hosts, no consumer
   file needs an import-path edit, and the public-surface gate passes.
3. `fetcher.types.ts` contains **only** type/interface declarations and
   `fetcher.args.ts` contains only the arg/exec primitives — no fetch function
   moves here.
4. Both new modules import only concrete siblings (never the `./fetcher.js`
   barrel); `fetcher.args.ts` may import types from `./fetcher.types.js` with
   `import type` only, so the cycle gate stays green.
5. The unmodified suites that exercise these primitives
   (`setWorklogDir.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`, `fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts`,
   `fetcher-timeout.test.ts`) pass, as does the full `packages/herdr` suite
   (`/skill:test`).
6. Each new module carries a one-line module doc comment naming its single
   responsibility; the original section banners and work-item ids move with
   their code.
7. `git diff` shows relocation, import rewiring and re-exports only — no logic

# Finalise fetcher barrel, docs and close-out

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
**Scope:** the residual `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` content (module doc
comment + import/export wiring) plus documentation updates and the final
verification pass for the epic.

## Goal

As a consumer of the fetcher, I want `fetcher.ts` to be a thin, honest barrel
that re-exports exactly the symbols other modules actually use, and I want the
herdr docs to show the module layout, so that the public surface is
discoverable and the epic's acceptance criteria are verifiable in one pass.

## Scope

- Reduce `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` to: a module-level doc comment (kept
  provenance, trimmed to a short overview + pointer to the module layout) and
  `export … from './fetcher.*.js'` statements only.
- Re-export **only the 42 symbols actually imported by consumers** (the frozen
  baseline from child 1); symbols that no consumer and no sibling module uses
  become internal.
- Empty the `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` in `fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` so the size gate
  now covers every `fetcher*.ts` module including the barrel.
- Documentation: add a "Module layout" section to
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (or the most relevant herdr doc)
  listing module → single responsibility → key exports; update
  `packages/herdr/README.md` if it names fetcher internals; fix any code
  comments that still describe the monolith.
- Record the final verification evidence on the epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wc -l packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ≤ 250, and the file contains no
   function/type/const declarations — only the doc comment and re-exports.
2. The barrel re-exports exactly the 42 consumer-imported symbols from the
   baseline, and no symbol that neither a consumer nor a sibling module imports;
   a scan comparing barrel exports against the baseline (plus sibling-module
   imports) is recorded as evidence.
3. `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is empty and the split-guard test proves every
   `packages/herdr/src/fetcher*.ts` production module (including the barrel) is
   ≤1,000 lines; the allowlist-shrink assertion is satisfied.
4. The split-guard public-surface, size, cycle and barrel-value-import gates all
   pass; no split module imports the barrel at runtime.
5. All 52 fetcher-related test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass
   **unmodified**, and the full repo suite passes (`/skill:test` full).
6. The relevant `docs/dev/*.md` contains a "Module layout" section listing every
   module created by the split with its single responsibility, and no doc or
   comment still refers to `fetcher.ts` as a 2,365-line monolith; a search of
   the repository docs confirms no other page documents the old internal layout
   (result recorded in the evidence comment).
7. The build is green (`npm run build` in `packages/herdr`) and `tsc` reports
   no new errors.
8. A comment on this item records: `wc -l` output for every module, the guard
   test output, the suite result, and the symbol → module mapping — enough to
   audit epic AC1–AC5 without re-running anything.
9. Every epic AC (1–5) is verified with the evidence above; any AC that cannot
   be met is raised as an OPEN QUESTION on the epic instead of being silently
   waived.

## Minimal implementation

1. Delete the remaining moved code from `fetcher.ts`; build the barrel export
   list from the baseline JSON (and sibling-module imports) so it is exactly the
   used surface.
2. Empty `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST`; run the guard suite and inspect each gate's output.
3. Rewrite the module doc comment: short overview, the fail-open contract and a
   pointer to the module-layout table in the docs.
4. Add the docs module-layout section; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it
   references internals.
5. Run `/skill:test` (full) + build; record the evidence comment; verify
   epic AC1–AC5.
6. Verify moved blocks match the pre-split source
   (`git show <pre-split>:packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` diff review) and note
   the result.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — becomes the thin barrel
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` — allowlist emptied

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the `src/github-sync.ts` split contract enforced by a machine gate **before** any production code moves, so the 1,000-line ceiling, the frozen public surface and an acyclic import graph cannot silently rot during the extraction.

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF — decompose `src/github-sync.ts`
**Position:** child 1 of 8 — lands first (test-first).

## Context

`src/github-sync.ts` is 1,339 lines and exports 6 types + 3 functions. The
shipped `src/sync.ts` guard (`tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts`,
WL-0MVP9MSJO0099V0G) and the in-progress `src/github.ts` guard
(`tests/github/github-split-guard-scan.ts`, WL-0MVVLXSQX0031IB3) already
provide reusable, parametrised scanners. This child reuses them — it must not
copy the parser.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/github-sync/split-guard-scan.ts` provides the github-sync family
   predicate (`src/github-sync.ts` + `src/github-sync/**`) and gate predicates,
   importing the parser/graph/export-kind scanners from
   `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` with the family and barrel parametrised.
2. `tests/github-sync/github-sync.split-baseline.json` freezes the public
   surface with provenance: 6 type exports (`SyncedItem`, `SyncErrorItem`,
   `GithubSyncResult`, `GithubSyncTiming`, `GithubProgress`, `FieldChange`) and
   4 value exports (`upsertIssuesFromWorkItems`, `resolveLabelField`,
   `resolveAllLabelFields`, `importIssuesToWorkItems`). The scanner output is
   the source of truth: record exactly what it reports.
3. `tests/github-sync/split-guard.test.ts` passes and proves each gate fails
   on deliberately broken input: an oversized module, a dropped export, a
   reclassified export, a runtime barrel import, a static cycle and a missing
   leading module JSDoc.
4. The size gate uses `MAX_MODULE_LINES = 1000` with a shrink-only allowlist
   whose ceiling is `['github-sync.ts']`; the barrel is allowlisted at plan
   time (1,339 lines) and no other module is.
5. The guard files carry leading JSDoc headers naming their concern, and the
   suite runs under the normal test runner without touching existing tests.
6. Public exports from the original module path remain importable unchanged
   (barrel re-export where consumers exist): the baseline freezes all six
   types and four functions, and the gate fails if any is dropped or
   reclassified.

   static and runtime import graphs are acyclic, and every family module opens
   with a JSDoc header naming its concern.

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `src/commands/init.ts` split, I want one automated
gate that fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so
that every extraction child can land safely, no existing test assertion changes,
and no reviewer has to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4 require: no file over 1,000 lines, an unchanged public
surface at `./init.js`, unmodified test assertions, and an acyclic import graph.
Nothing in the repo enforces this for `src/commands/init*.ts` today. This child

(WL-0MVP9MSJO0099V0G) and `tests/interview/split-guard.test.ts`
(WL-0MVXY34A900816MN).

Facts captured at plan time (2026-11-03, `dev`):

- `src/commands/init.ts` — 1,515 lines; public surface is exactly

  `isSorraAgentsInstalled(): boolean`.

# Parse the proxy's slots_detail_stale and slot_counts_stale flags

## Problem statement

`parseLlamaStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts`) reads only
one staleness flag — `slots_stale` — from `GET {proxyUrl}/llama/local/status`.
The proxy serves **three** independent staleness flags, and the two the worker
ignores are the ones that say *which part* of the payload is untrustworthy:

| Proxy field | Meaning | Parsed today |
|---|---|---|
| `slots_stale` | the per-slot detail cannot be paired with the counts | yes → `usablePerSlotSlots()` fails closed |
| `slots_detail_stale` | the detail itself is a last-known snapshot | **no** |
| `slot_counts_stale` | the counts (`available_slots`/`total_slots`) are last-known | **no** |

Consequence: herdr collapses three distinct proxy degradations into one opaque
`slots-unavailable` refusal, so the decision log cannot distinguish "the proxy's
`/slots` query is failing" from "only the counts are cached while the detail is
fresh". During the 2026-11-04 overnight outage the proxy served
`slots_stale: true` together with `slots_detail_stale: true` and
`slot_counts_stale: false` (detail stale, counts fresh) for eight hours — an
8-hour-old frozen snapshot
(`slots_snapshot_age_seconds≈29,057`, `slots_snapshot_source=snapshot`,
`slot_id=unknown`, `measured_cache=0` in the proxy log) — and none of that
distinction reached the decision log or the herdr header.

Similarly `local_abandoned_slots` (served as `2` in that incident, while both
cached slots were frozen `is_processing: true, abandoned: true`) is unparsed, so
the evidence that the snapshot was internally contradictory never reached the
decision entry.

## Goal

A capacity refusal caused by untrustworthy slot data is *attributable* from the
decision log and header alone: the record says which signal was stale, without
reading the proxy's own log on another host.

User story: "As an on-call maintainer triaging a 'nothing dispatched' night, I
want the decision entry to tell me whether the counts, the per-slot detail, or
both were cached, so I can tell a proxy-side observability failure from genuine
GPU saturation."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Both flags are parsed.** `parseLlamaStatus` parses `slots_detail_stale` and
   `slot_counts_stale` with the same optional-boolean contract already used for
   `slots_stale`: absent → `undefined` (pre-feature proxy, behaviour unchanged);
   non-boolean → reject the poll (fail-closed, ambiguous); present → carried on
   `LlamaStatus`.
2. **Refusals stay fail-closed.** Availability is unchanged: `slots` usable only
   when non-empty **and** not `slots_stale`; the count-based fallback stays
   removed. The new flags are evidence, never an alternative budget.
3. **Attribution reaches the decision log.** Every `slots-unavailable` decision
   entry carries the observed flags as additive fields (for example
   `slotsDetailStale`, `slotCountsStale`), following the existing additive
   evidence convention (`auditBatchDepth`, reservation evidence). Entries keep
   their shape when the proxy is pre-feature.
4. **Header token distinguishes, or documents why not.** Either the herdr header
   blocking token distinguishes the stale-detail case from a plain unusable
   payload, or the item records why a single token is retained (with the reason
   in the code comment and the docs).
5. **`local_abandoned_slots` is carried as advisory evidence** on the decision
   entry, so a self-contradictory proxy snapshot (counts say free, detail says
   all slots busy/abandoned) is visible in the record.
6. **Contradictory payload is covered by a test.** A payload with
   `available_slots > 0`, `capacity_hint: "idle"` and all cached slots
   `is_processing: true` never admits a dispatch and records the new evidence
   fields.
7. **Docs updated.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (fail-closed contract /
   decision-log schema) lists the new fields and what each flag means for
   diagnosis.
8. **Full project test suite passes** (`/skill:test`).

## Plan

1. Extend the optional-boolean parsing (reuse the `slots_stale` shape) and add
   the fields to `LlamaStatus`; unit tests for absent / valid / malformed.
   → verify: `downtime-worker.test.ts` parser table extended and green.
2. Thread the flags into `capacityEvidence`/`recordDecision` for the
   `slots-unavailable` path (and `capacity-saturated` where relevant).
   → verify: `downtime-worker.leaf-audit.test.ts` / orchestration tests assert
   the fields on the emitted entry.
3. Cover the contradictory-payload case end-to-end; no dispatch, evidence
   recorded.
   → verify: new test failing before the change, green after.
4. Update the docs schema table and the fail-closed section.
   → verify: docs test / manual check, then `/skill:test` full.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts` (`parseLlamaStatus`, optional
  boolean helpers).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` (`LlamaStatus`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts` (`usablePerSlotSlots`, unchanged
  semantics — availability must not broaden).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` (`capacityEvidence`,
  decision header tokens).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` (`slots-unavailable`
  refusals).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Risks & notes

- **Do not relax the fail-closed contract.** The temptation is to treat "counts
  fresh, detail stale" as a usable signal. It is not: an 8-hour-old detail with
  a fresh count is exactly what starved dispatch for a night. Evidence only.
- **Malformed-flag strictness.** The existing contract rejects the whole poll on
  a malformed availability-affecting flag. Keep that for these two flags, and
  note the drift risk with the proxy team (the proxy has previously emitted
  "not computable" nulls for advisory fields; availability-affecting counters
  must stay numeric).
- **Additive-only log shape.** Decision entries must remain backward compatible
  for existing readers and for `hourlyReasonTally`.

## Related

- RCA: overnight zero-dispatch incident, 2026-11-03T20:51Z → 2026-11-04T08:30Z;
  proxy served a frozen 8-hour slot snapshot (`slots_stale`,
  `slots_detail_stale`) and herdr failed closed with `slots-unavailable`.
- WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW — fail-closed `slots-unavailable` contract (this item adds
  attribution only).
- LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ — llm-manager proxy-side improvement (serve fresh per-slot
  detail; the upstream defect is tracked and being fixed there).
- WL-0MVKNC2N50025HXE — capacity-starvation / long-running pane observation.

# Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in ContextHub

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (0)

_None — only hooks below are pending._

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

## Provenance

Created from the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA. Pi session `herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004`, log `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-11-04T07-55-10-163Z_herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004.jsonl`.
