# Generalise the host dispatch budget to any work item type

## Problem Statement

The host-wide dispatch budget (`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`,
parent WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB) only covers two kinds: `implement` and `audit`.
`budget.json` is a fixed two-field shape (`{ "maxImplement": 2, "maxAudit": 1 }`),
the `HostBudgetKind` type is `'implement' | 'audit'`, and the interactive
over-quota dialog (`budgetKindForAgentCommand`) recognises only those two.
Capping `plan`, `intake` or `risk-effort` dispatches is currently impossible —
it was explicitly recorded as out of scope in the v1 contract (F6,
WL-0MVXY10QH0020V7S: "Capping the `plan` / `intake` / `risk-effort` tiers is
likewise out of scope").

Operators want one machine-scoped concurrency governor that can cap any kind
of dispatched work, with the same semantics the implement/audit tiers already
have — and they want it to be a general mechanism, not N special cases.

## Users

- **Operators.** As a herdr operator, I want to set a host-wide concurrency
  cap for any dispatch kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`,
  `risk-effort`), so that I can bound the machine's agent work-in-flight per
  kind — and leave any kind unlimited by simply not configuring it.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the dispatch admission path, I want one generic
  budget check for every kind, so plan/intake/risk-effort dispatches are
  subject to the same host-wide constraints (and the same observability) as
  implement/audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Any kind configurable.** `budget.json` accepts a cap for every dispatch
   kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`). A cap set
   for any kind is enforced at admission (refuse when live >= cap) on both
   dispatcher paths (direct and coordination leader), with `0` remaining the
   per-kind kill switch.
2. **Absent = unlimited.** A kind not explicitly present in the budget config
   is **unlimited**: admission never refuses it on budget grounds, it is never
   counted against any cap, and its dispatches are not recorded in the ledger
   (no reserve/release bookkeeping for uncapped kinds). No default cap is
   invented for unconfigured kinds.
3. **Existing budgets preserved.** The default stays `implement: 2`,
   `audit: 1`, and an operator's existing `budget.json` values keep their
   meaning and enforcement (same refusal behaviour, same kill switch) — the
   generalisation must not change or silently drop configured caps.
4. **Counting asymmetry preserved, audit-only.** Only `audit` keeps the
   over-hold semantics: it counts fresh ledger entries with **no** live-pane
   requirement (`freshCount` — slot held from reservation until a release
   point fires or the 2 h stale window). Every **other** kind counts only
   fresh entries whose pane is in the machine-wide live pane list
   (`liveCount`), so its slot frees when the pane leaves the live list.
5. **Legacy code removed (no backward compatibility).** The following are
   deleted, not kept behind compat shims:
   - the retired `active-audit` marker readers (`readActiveAuditMarker`,
     `isHostAuditActive` in `machine-coordination.ts`) and the synthetic
     legacy-marker entry count (`legacyActiveAuditCount` / `reduceMarkerCounts`);
   - the `audit-host-saturated` token special-case at `maxAudit: 1`
     (unified to the single `host-budget-audit` refusal token);
   - the fixed two-kind `HostBudgetKind` type and `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG`
     shape; the fixed two-key env overrides (`HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` /
     `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT`) are generalised or removed;
   - any F6 doc carve-out text describing plan/intake/risk-effort as out of
     scope.
   A repo-wide scan confirms no references to the removed symbols remain
   (module headers, doc comments and the `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
   contract of record updated to match).
6. **Interactive over-quota gate generalised.** A hand-fired
   `/skill:<kind>` dispatch for any capped kind consults the same ledger/cap
   and prompts on over-quota, exactly as implement/audit do today
   (`budgetKindForAgentCommand` generalised to all kinds).
7. **Observability generalised.** The worklist header counter, stderr skip
   line and decision-log tokens report live/max **per configured kind**
   (any capped kind), never for uncapped kinds; an uncapped kind can never
   produce a budget refusal token.
8. **Tests.** Unit + integration tests cover: capped plan/intake/risk-effort
   admit and refuse at their caps; an uncapped kind always admits and records
   nothing; per-kind kill switch `0`; audit over-hold vs live-pane release
   for all other kinds; refusal tokens unified (no `audit-host-saturated`
   anywhere); legacy-marker references gone; existing implement/audit
   behaviour with the default config unchanged. Full project suite passes.

## Constraints

- Scope: `packages/herdr` only (ledger, admission, interactive gate,
  observability, machine-coordination). No worklog (`wl`) / database scoring
  changes; the dispatcher head remains the sole ranking path.
- `scheduled` prompts are **not** a work-item kind and stay outside the
  budget; the budget covers `DowntimeSkillKind` only.
- The budget remains the **outer** concurrency governor: the inner capacity
  gates (free-slot minimums, local reservation/prefill pacing, contention,
  host-CPU gate) keep their existing order and meaning.
- No `window`/rate-limit field (explicitly still out of scope in v1).

## Existing State

- `HostBudgetKind = 'implement' | 'audit'` (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`),
  `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG = { maxImplement: 2, maxAudit: 1 }`, clamps
  `0..HOST_BUDGET_MAX (32)`, env overrides `HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` /
  `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT`.
- Counting: implement uses `liveCount` (live-pane), audit uses `freshCount`
  (marker semantics, incl. the synthetic legacy-marker entry).
- Admission in `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`
  (`admitHostDispatch` / `readAuditBudgetState` / `confirmHostDispatch` /
  `releaseHostDispatch`); interactive gate in
  `host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`; refuse tokens
  `host-budget-implement` / `host-budget-audit` / `host-budget-unknown` plus
  the `audit-host-saturated` compat token.
- The removal of the legacy `active-audit` readers was already scheduled for
  "the release after the host-wide budget generalisation ships"
  (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, F6 removal schedule) — this item is
  that release.
- `DowntimeSkillKind = 'plan' | 'intake' | 'audit' | 'implement' |
  'risk-effort'`; dispatch-classified kinds today are `audit`, `implement`,
  `plan`, `intake` (intake → plan → implement chain) and `risk-effort`
  (effort/risk evaluation for plan_complete items).

## Desired Change

1. Generalise `HostBudgetKind` to all `DowntimeSkillKind` members; the config
   becomes a map over kinds (absent kind ⇒ uncapped). Keep `implement: 2`,
   `audit: 1` as the defaults for those kinds.
2. Admission becomes one generic path: look up the kind's cap; absent ⇒ admit
   without reservation; present ⇒ the existing live-count admission with the
   audit over-hold exception (`freshCount` for `audit` only).
3. Delete the legacy-marker surface and unify the refusal tokens on
   `host-budget-*`.
4. Extend `budgetKindForAgentCommand` and the over-quota dialog to all kinds.
5. Generalise the observability surfaces (counter, skip line, decision tokens)
   to list every configured kind; uncapped kinds never appear.
6. Update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (module tables, gate table,
   removal schedule, out-of-scope wording) and all affected module doc
   comments.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — kind type, config schema,
  live/fresh counting, reap, kill switch
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — generic admission,
  refusal tokens, audit over-hold
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` /
  `host-budget-dialog.ts` — over-quota gate + dialog for all kinds
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — remove legacy marker readers
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — generalised counter/skip line
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — refusal-token mapping
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — contract of record update
- Tests: `host-dispatch-budget*.test.ts`, `host-budget-dialog*.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`, machine tests

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (recorded):** "Keep the configured budget for any existing
  items in place" means the default caps (`implement: 2`, `audit: 1`) and any
  operator-written `budget.json` values remain honoured exactly; the
  generalisation may change the on-disk schema but must preserve the effective
  caps and enforcement for `implement` and `audit`.
- **Assumption (recorded):** uncapped kinds bypass the ledger entirely (no
  reserve/release entries) — simplest semantics for "not limited"; the
  pane-close release is idempotent by item id and unaffected for capped kinds.
- Risk: generalising the admission seam touches the dispatch choke point;
  mitigated by keeping the counting asymmetry behaviour-preserving for
  implement/audit and by the test matrix (AC8).
- Risk: observability surfaces must not regress for existing kinds — the
  unified `host-budget-audit` token replaces `audit-host-saturated`, so any
  operator tooling keyed on the old token must be updated in the same change.

## Related Work

- WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB (completed) — parent: host-wide concurrency budget for
  implement and audit dispatches (this item extends it)
- WL-0MVXY0XPF006YUHA (completed) — F2 audit 1→N generalisation + active-audit
  unification, which scheduled the legacy-marker removal this item performs
- WL-0MVXY0WQF0069YDJ / WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI / WL-0MVXY0Z93002HKCZ /
  WL-0MVXY0ZYW009NEJD / WL-0MVXY10QH0020V7S / WL-0MVXY11IL0032S07
  (completed) — F1–F7 slices of the original budget work

---
*Created from a user request to extend the budget workflow to any work item
type, with unlimited default for unconfigured kinds, no backward-compatibility
requirement (dead code removal permitted), existing budgets preserved, and the
over-hold approach retained for audit only.*
data.title: Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type (absent = unlimited, audit-only over-hold)

# Dispatcher claims work items as 'dispatcher' instead of producer sentinel 'Map'

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher claims every work item it auto-dispatches with the
producer sentinel `Map`, so an auto-dispatched claim is indistinguishable from a
deliberate producer hold. Agent sessions preserve it at exit, the TTL reaper never
reaps it, and the item is stranded as a scheduling hold with no agent working.

Observed on WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y: the herdr worker claimed it with `Map` at intake
dispatch (02:06 UTC) and again at plan dispatch (~13:03 UTC). The plan session
completed (stage `plan_complete`, status `open`) but deliberately restored `Map`
believing it was a producer hold. The item has stayed invisible to dispatch ever
since (`wl next` skips held items; the all-held dispatch window is only surfaced
read-only, WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs auto-dispatched work to keep flowing after a
  session ends; a stranded `Map` claim silently stalls the queue.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher** — claims items before spawning agent panes; needs
  an identity that means "an agent is on it", not "the producer parked it".
- **Agent sessions (intake/plan/implement/audit/risk-effort)** — release their own
  claims at session end; must release a dispatcher claim exactly like an agent
  claim, while never touching a genuine producer hold.
- **Auditor / reviewer** — relies on `needsProducerReview` and the `Map` hold as
  the only two legitimate reasons an item is intentionally held.

Example user stories:

- As the producer, when the dispatcher claims an item and the session ends without
  completing it, the item becomes dispatchable again instead of vanishing.
- As an agent session, I preserve a `Map` producer hold at exit but clear a
  `dispatcher` claim, so I never strand auto-dispatched work.
- As the downtime worker, I can distinguish "held by the producer on purpose" from
  "claimed by me moments ago" without reading the source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` claims auto-dispatched items with `dispatcher` (replacing `AGENT_ASSIGNEE = 'Map'`), for every dispatch tier (audit, implement, plan, intake, risk-effort) and every dispatch path that uses `claimWorkItem` / `claimItem`.
- **AC2**: An assignee of `dispatcher` is not a scheduling hold: `wl next` / dispatch gates / the herdr assignee-hold filter (`downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` / `downtime-worker.selection.ts` `isAssigneeHeld`) never skip an item merely because its assignee is `dispatcher`.
- **AC3**: Agent sessions release the `dispatcher` claim on every terminal outcome — the shared `should_release_assignee` predicate and `release_session_claim` / `reap_stale_claims` backstops treat `dispatcher` as releasable (it is not a protected producer hold).
- **AC4**: A genuine producer hold (`Map` / `WORKLOG_PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE`) remains sacrosanct: never released, never reaped, still a scheduling hold. Existing behaviour for `Map` is unchanged.
- **AC5**: The producer-assignee sentinel and the dispatcher claim identity are defined once each in code (configurable or a shared constant) so the two concepts cannot drift again; the collision is documented in code comments at both call sites.
- **AC6**: Tests cover: dispatcher claims record `dispatcher`; a `dispatcher`-held item is still dispatchable / not held; a `dispatcher` claim is released by `should_release_assignee` and by the session backstop; a `Map` producer hold is still preserved; the all-held-window attribution no longer counts `dispatcher` as a hold.
- **AC7**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `AGENTS.md` / the global agent instructions, and `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` / `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- **AC8**: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; no regression in the herdr dispatch/offer suites.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo scope.** The herdr claim identity lives in this repository (ContextHub, `packages/herdr`). The shared Python release predicate (`skill/shared/claim_release.py` — `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT`, `is_producer_assignee`, `should_release_assignee`, `release_session_claim`, `reap_stale_claims`) is agent infrastructure that in this checkout resolves through `skill/shared -> ~/.pi/agent/skills/shared`, i.e. the **SorraAgents** repository. `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` also live in SorraAgents. The fix therefore spans two repositories, and the ContextHub item may need a posed, blocking SorraAgents companion item for the Python-side predicate, docs and release invariant wording.
- Do not weaken any safety gate: `dispatcher` is only ever the claim identity, never a bypass. `needsProducerReview` and producer-hold semantics stay exactly as-is.
- The agent-side release logic (skill/shared) is shared infrastructure — prefer a single predicate that knows both identities (`dispatcher` releasable, `Map` protected), rather than a second ad-hoc check.
- Keep existing `Map` producer-hold behaviour byte-for-byte; treat any change to `Map` semantics as a regression.
- Do not edit agent infrastructure under `.pi/` or the symlinked `skill/shared` unless the cross-repo work is explicitly authorised in the SorraAgents checkout.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` — `const AGENT_ASSIGNEE = 'Map'`; used by `claimItemForAgentCommand` (`claimWorkItem(itemId, AGENT_ASSIGNEE)`) and re-exported.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1589` — `createDowntimeDeps(SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT, AGENT_ASSIGNEE)` feeds the same constant into the downtime claim path (`deps.claimItem`), so the dispatcher and interactive claims currently share the `Map` identity.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — the claim → marker → spawn pipeline; `claimItem` CAS semantics; no assignee policy of its own.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `isAssigneeHeld` treats **any** non-empty assignee as a hold (`.filter((c) => !isAssigneeHeld(c))` in every dispatch candidate path).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — classifies every all-held window solely on a non-empty assignee, with `heldAssignees` (e.g. `['Map']`).
- `skill/shared/claim_release.py` (SorraAgents) — `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT = "Map"`, `is_producer_assignee`, `should_release_assignee`; `release_session_claim` and `reap_stale_claims` never touch a producer hold.
- Tests currently hard-code `'Map'` in many dispatch/offer suites (`claim.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `dispatch-window-hold.test.ts`, `worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`) — these encode the current, incorrect assumption and will need review.

## Desired change

Introduce a distinct `dispatcher` claim identity. The dispatcher claims with
`dispatcher`; an assignee of `dispatcher` is released on every terminal outcome
and is **not** a scheduling hold, so the dispatch gates/offer attribution must
not treat it as held. Keep `Map` (and `WORKLOG_PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE`) as the only
protected producer hold. Define both identities once so they cannot drift, and
document the collision at both call sites and in the release-invariant docs.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — regression in dispatch gating.** Relaxing `isAssigneeHeld` for `dispatcher` touches the hot path of every candidate filter; mitigate by keeping the predicate single-sourced and adding a test per dispatch path. Residual risk: a `dispatcher` string typo could still be read as a hold, so define the identity as one exported constant.
- **Risk — cross-repo drift.** The Python predicate (SorraAgents) and the TypeScript constant (ContextHub) could disagree about which identities are releasable; mitigate by keeping the sentinel/identity definitions and the collision comment in both places, and by linking the companion SorraAgents item as a blocker.
- **Risk — masked stale claims.** If the dispatcher is killed before a session starts, a `dispatcher` claim could be reaped by the TTL sweep mid-dispatch; the reaper's non-terminal/TTL guard is assumed sufficient (same behaviour as any agent claim).
- **Assumption:** `dispatcher` does not collide with a real agent or producer identity, and is not a value `WORKLOG_PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE` is expected to take.
- **Assumption:** existing `Map` producer-hold behaviour must be preserved exactly; any behavioural change to `Map` is out of scope and a regression.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a wider producer-hold retirement or a general hold-bucket taxonomy is *not* part of this item. Record such opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` — replace `AGENT_ASSIGNEE = 'Map'` with the dispatcher identity; use a shared constant
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps(...)` wiring; update comments
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — dispatch claim identity if it is threaded separately

- SorraAgents: `skill/shared/claim_release.py` — `should_release_assignee` / `is_producer_assignee` knows `dispatcher` is releasable
- SorraAgents: `docs/dev/assignee-release.md`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, and this repo's `AGENTS.md` — release-invariant wording gains the `dispatcher` identity
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher claim identity documentation

## Related work

- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y** — Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no running herdr instance (stranded at `plan_complete` with a lingering `Map` dispatcher claim). This item is `discovered-from` that one.

- **WL-0MVAPF19Q0096EP0** — Theme/interview/shortcuts restore + producer-hold retirement. Completed.
- Potentially related docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `CLI.md`, and SorraAgents' `docs/dev/assignee-release.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Duplicate-work check** — Searched `wl search "dispatcher claim assignee Map"`. Closest completed items (WL-0MV85WDOM007BKF8, WL-0MV85WESL002SD0F, WL-0MVAPF19Q0096EP0) define the producer-hold convention and release gate, but none fixes the dispatcher's use of `Map` as its claim identity. # herdr extension key chords to set a work item's assignee

Add herdr worklist key chords (same mechanism as the existing `c q` quick-create chord —
`packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` / `loadShortcutConfig`, worklist input loop) that
set the focused work item's assignee to one of the three hold identities, or clear it:

- `a p` — assignee = `producer`
- `a a` — assignee = `agent`
- `a n` — clear the assignee (`--assignee ""`)
- `a d` — assignee = `dispatcher`

## Goal

Give the operator one-key access to the scheduling-hold semantics that drive dispatch:
setting a producer hold, tagging an agent claim, clearing a stale hold, or (after
WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG) marking an item as dispatcher-handled — without hand-editing via CLI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: The four chords (`a p` / `a a` / `a n` / `a d`) are registered in the herdr
  shortcut config for the worklist view and work on the focused item.
- **AC2**: Each chord runs `wl update <id> --assignee <value>` (or the equivalent
  worklog-dir-safe update) against the focused item; `a n` clears the assignee.
- **AC3**: The updates flow through the standard command/refresh path (a completion-refresh
  re-renders the worklist, mirroring chord-quick-create).
- **AC4**: Chord conflicts are handled: the second keys (`p`, `a`, `n`, `d`) must not collide
  with existing handlers (quit-key case documented in chord-quick-create).
- **AC5**: The chords are documented in the herdr README / CLI.md keybinding reference, with
  the hold semantics of each identity (`producer` = persistent hold, `agent` = session claim,
  `dispatcher` = non-hold after WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG, empty = dispatchable).
- **AC6**: Unit tests drive the real worklist input loop with the production shortcut registry
  for all four chords (same harness as chord-quick-create.test.ts), asserting the dispatched
  `wl update` command and assignee value.
- **AC7**: Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Notes

- The `dispatcher` identity is a scheduling NON-hold only after WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG lands;
  until then `a d` would create a hold — sequence or gate the chord so it matches the
  dispatcher-claim semantics at the time it is used (document the pre/post state).
- Follow the settings/shortcut validation pattern in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.

## Related Work

- discovered-from: WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y — Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no
  running herdr instance (the stack that exposed how opaque the assignee/hold machine is).
- WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG — Dispatcher claims work items as 'dispatcher' instead of producer
  sentinel 'Map' (critical; defines the `dispatcher` identity this chord writes).
- WL-0MTCLB50D0026YA7 — the `c q` quick-create chord this work mirrors.

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — chord registry

  loop and focused-item resolution

# Herdr session-path round-trip tests fail under a hyphenated TMPDIR

## Problem statement

Two tests in `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` fail whenever the ambient
`TMPDIR` contains a hyphen:

- `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath decodes a pi session dir back to the worklog root`
- `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver falls back to the pi session path when cwd is absent`

Both build their fixture root with `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'stallroot'))`
and then encode it the way Pi encodes a session directory (every `/` replaced
by `-`) before asserting that `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath` decodes it back.
The encoding is **lossy for any hyphen** in the path, so the assertion can only
hold when the whole root is hyphen-free — the test comment even says so
("Hyphen-free prefix so the pi session-path encoding ... round-trips
unambiguously"), but the *prefix* is hyphen-free while `tmpdir()` is not.

The test skill's runner now injects a disk-backed `TMPDIR`
(`/var/tmp/pi-test-<uid>`, SA-0MW3ENF32006BGN1) — hyphenated by construction —
so both tests fail on every agent-driven run:

```
x worklogRootFromPiSessionPath decodes a pi session dir back to the worklog root
  expected undefined to be '/var/tmp/pi-test-1000/stallroothPRXF4'
x defaultStalledPaneRootResolver falls back to the pi session path when cwd is absent
  expected null to be '/var/tmp/pi-test-1000/stallrootiznmd1'
```

## Impact

`packages/herdr/**` is a declared changed-scope test group, so any change that
touches herdr selects `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` as the
implement-finish gate — which is now red for an unrelated, environment-only
reason. Workaround in use: `PI_TEST_TMPDIR=/tmp/<hyphen-free>`. The dev-push
pre-push gate (`npm --silent test -- tests`) does not include this group, so a
push is not blocked, but the changed-scope gate is.

Reproduced on `dev` at 4d105bf8 with no local changes, both in the main
checkout and in a linked worktree: 2 failed tests; green with
`PI_TEST_TMPDIR=/tmp/pitestwork`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` no longer depends on `tmpdir()` being
      hyphen-free: the round-trip assertions pass under a hyphenated
      `TMPDIR` (e.g. `TMPDIR=/var/tmp/pi-test-1000`) as well as a hyphen-free one.
- [ ] The test keeps asserting the real decode contract for a hyphen-free root
      (no silent `skip` that removes the coverage on the machines that run it).
- [ ] `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` is green under the test skill's
      default disk-backed `TMPDIR` (no `PI_TEST_TMPDIR` override).
- [ ] Record which side owns the durable fix (this repo's test fixture vs the
      test skill's `pi-test-<uid>` TMPDIR naming, SorraAgents) and link the
      companion item if one is needed.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — `makeRoot()` and the two session-path
  round-trip assertions (stalled-work production wiring block).

## Related work

- `discovered-from:WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO` — the hyphenated-TMPDIR failures were
  found while running that item's changed-scope gate.
- WL-0MUYMBSA90092QV2 — introduced the stalled-work production wiring (and these
  two tests).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/cli/inproc-harness-budget.test.ts > in-process harness budget: measured guard > re-measures the four scenarios inside the budget (bounded, read-only)
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
AssertionError: per-call cost exceeded the budget: list-json 33.92 ms > 17.67 ms, create 47.45 ms > 18.86 ms, status 36.82 ms > 14.99 ms (loadFactor 1.07)
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k 'tests/cli/inproc-harness-budget.test.ts > in-process harness budget: measured guard > re-measures the four scenarios inside the budget (bounded, read-only)'` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/cli/inproc-harness-budget.test.ts > in-process harness budget: measured guard > re-measures the four scenarios inside the budget (bounded, read-only)` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Diagnosis

The guard measures the per-call wall cost of four in-process `wl` scenarios and compares it against `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` × (1 + headroom) × a host-load factor derived from `os.loadavg()[0]`.

The failure is **host-contention noise, not a regression**:

- On a quiet host (load ≈ 0.4) the same profile with the capture's warmup methodology measures `help 1.96 / list-json 4.42 / create 4.76 / status 3.26 ms` — `0.81–0.94×` the recorded baselines.
- The measured test passed `warmupRuns: 0` (the artefact is captured with one discarded warmup) and `runs: 3`, so its median includes the cold first call.
- The load factor is sampled from `os.loadavg()[0]` once at the end; under the suite's parallel workers it reads low while the short measurement is genuinely descheduled/I-O-contended, so the factor stays 1 and the inflated wall time trips the limit.
- CPU time is **not** a usable load-independent alternative here: under the same contention the `create`/`list-json` scenarios' CPU time also inflates (up to 3–4×; libuv threadpool + kernel time), so a CPU gate would flake too.

## Fix

Keep the wall + load-factor policy, and make the *measurement* robust:

- Use the capture methodology (`warmupRuns: 1`, `runs: 5`) so the median excludes the cold call and matches the recorded baseline.
- Re-measure up to a small bounded number of attempts and judge the **best** attempt; a genuine order-of-magnitude regression fails every attempt, while a transient contention spike no longer flakes the guard.
- Keep the guard's own cost bounded well inside the existing 5 s budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The measured guard uses the artefact's capture methodology (one discarded warmup, `runs >= 3`) and re-measures up to a bounded number of attempts, judging the best attempt.
- A genuine order-of-magnitude regression still fails (the synthetic policy test pins the limit maths and pass/fail behaviour).
- The guard's own elapsed cost stays within its 5 s budget (asserted).
- The guard no longer fails on host contention: verified locally under an artificial CPU load, and by the dev-push full-suite gate.
- The test's header documentation explains the best-of-N/warmup methodology and why CPU time is not the gate.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/inproc-harness-budget.test.ts` — measured guard: warmup + bounded best-of-N attempts; header rationale.

# Implement left-of-extensions tab placement for interactive dispatches

## Summary

Add an interactive-placement mode to the tab-creation path so operator-created tabs appear left of the Worklog/extensions tab; dispatcher tabs remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An interactive dispatch that creates a new tab (ID-carrying commands such as `/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, prompt/`!!`/`!` commands carrying a work-item ID, and a new-pi-session dispatch from the selection list) places that tab immediately to the left of the Worklog (extensions/plugin) tab in the invoking workspace.
- Automated dispatches (downtime dispatcher) place their tabs at the default right-side position exactly as today — no behaviour change.
- Tab repositioning is implemented via the herdr socket API `tab.move` with `insert_index` set to the extensions tab's index (or an equivalent herdr CLI/socket mechanism available at implement time); the tab is first created as today and then moved.
- Fail-open: when the Worklog/extensions tab cannot be resolved (no plugin pane, no tab labelled `Worklog`, multiple/ambiguous matches) or `tab.move` fails, the newly created tab stays at its default right-side position — the dispatch is never blocked, dropped, or placed in a wrong workspace.
- Reuse semantics are preserved: an existing item-ID tab is adopted without being moved (only freshly provisioned tabs are repositioned; a reused tab's position is the operator's own arrangement).
- At least one automated test (unit or integration) covers each of: left placement for an interactively created tab, default right placement for a dispatcher-created tab, and fail-open when the extensions tab or the move is unavailable.

## Implementation approach

1. Add a `moveTabInWorkspace` helper to `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` using the herdr socket API (`tab.move` with `insert_index`).
2. Add a `resolveExtensionsTab` helper to `dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` that finds the extensions tab and returns its index, failing open on ambiguity.
3. Add a `placement` flag/param to `createTabInWorkspace` and `DispatcherAnchorDeps.createTab` (default `right`, new option `left-of-extensions`).
4. In `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` / `getItemTabAnchor` interactive provisioning path: when a fresh tab is created (signalled by `onCreate`), move it left of the extensions tab using the new helpers.

## Problem

The machine-scoped dispatch-budget ledger (`/home/rgardler/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json`, `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`) is holding an **audit** entry for `MS-0MW1ZSC7U000V5MW` (pane `w3G:p1B9`, heartbeat `2026-11-06T21:02:53Z`) whose pane no longer exists in `herdr pane list`. Because the audit tier counts fresh entries without a live-pane requirement (`freshCount`), the dead entry keeps the audit tier at its default `maxAudit: 1` cap until the 2 h staleness window expires.

## Incident evidence

Observed on 2026-11-06 while investigating WL-0MW5JE0SZ0057K30: the audit tier refused every `completed/in_review` candidate (`MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT`, `SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF`) for ~90 minutes after their audit pane had closed.

## Impact

Audit dispatch recovers as soon as an audit pane closes — the tier stops reporting a phantom in-progress audit and admits the next `completed/in_review` candidate immediately instead of stalling for up to two hours.

## Desired change

Release or reap an audit ledger entry when its pane closes (the `recordPaneClose` best-effort release is not firing on every close path), so a closed audit pane does not hold the audit cap for the remainder of the staleness window.

## Notes

- Distinct from WL-0MW5JE0SZ0057K30, which fixes the orphaned item-tab placeholder pane left when the budget refuses a dispatch.
- Related: WL-0MVXY0XPF006YUHA (audit tier / active-audit unification), WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI (implement-tier admission), WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB (generalise the budget).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A machine-ledger entry with a non-empty \`paneId\` that is absent from a trusted machine-wide live pane list is removed on the next pane-close-reaper pass regardless of heartbeat freshness, so a closed audit pane cannot hold \`maxAudit\` for the remainder of the 2 h staleness window.
- The pane-close reaper releases the item's host-dispatch ledger entry immediately after it closes that pane (implement and audit kinds), idempotently.
- Unconfirmed entries (no \`paneId\`, the reserve→spawn window) and entries whose pane is live are retained; no sweep is applied when the live pane list cannot be read (fail-safe: no over-reaping, no over-admission).
- Regression coverage: unit tests for the ledger sweep (dead / live / unconfirmed / stale), the reaper's post-close release and ledger-sweep seams (success, dry-run, failed close, throwing seam), and the \`createHerdrReaperDeps\` wiring.
- \`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md\` documents the ledger release points and the dead-pane sweep.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

- \`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts\` — new \`sweepClosedPanes\` (drop confirmed entries whose pane is absent, plus stale entries).
- \`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.test.ts\` — sweep unit tests.

# Inconsistent soft-delete predicate: `wl list` excludes only `status=deleted` while `wl update` rejects any non-empty `deletedBy`

## Problem statement

Two code paths disagree about what counts as "soft-deleted":

- **`wl list`** excludes a row only when `status === 'deleted'` (`src/commands/list.ts`, the `includeDeleted` filter). It ignores `deletedBy`.
- **`wl update`** refuses to mutate a row whenever `deletedBy` is non-empty, regardless of `status` (`src/commands/update.ts`, the soft-delete guard `SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9 AC1`, error code `deleted-item`). It ignores `status`.

The result is a row that is *both* visible and immutable:

- **visible** in `wl list --stage <X>` because its `status` is not `'deleted'`, and
- **immutable** because its `deletedBy` is set, so `wl update` rejects it as `deleted-item`.

## Impact

A soft-deleted-then-repaired item (e.g. `status=completed` with `deletedBy` retained to preserve deletion intent) that also carries `stage=in_review` shows up as a **release candidate** for `wl list --stage in_review`, but the audit runner's `wl update --status in_progress` fails with `deleted-item`. This blocks the `dev -> main` release gate (ship skill) for a row that is, by the CLI's own definition, deleted. It surfaced during the ship release attempt on 2026-11-06 (see MS-0MW22TQS8008021W), where four items had to be hand-repaired to clear `in_review` from the candidate list.

## Root cause

The two predicates are not derived from one shared definition of "soft-deleted":

| Path | Predicate | File / symbol |
|------|-----------|---------------|
| list | `item.status !== 'deleted'` | `src/commands/list.ts` — `includeDeleted` filter |
| update | `String(item.deletedBy ?? '').trim() !== ''` | `src/commands/update.ts` — soft-delete guard |

## Reproduction

1. Take a work item with `status=completed`, `stage=in_review`, and a non-empty `deletedBy` (e.g. any item repaired after a `wl delete`).
2. `wl list --stage in_review --json` → the item is returned as a candidate.
3. `wl update <id> --status in_progress --json` → `{ "success": false, "error": "deleted-item" }`.

Live evidence (tce-main-street store, 2026-11-08): the four items repaired during the ship run all have `status=completed`, `deletedBy=250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `stage=done`:

- `wl list --stage done --json` returns all four.
- `wl update MS-0MT3JK16W006A66P --title probe --json` returns `success:false, error:"deleted-item"`.

If their `stage` had remained `in_review`, they would have blocked the release gate exactly as described in the ship comment.

## Desired change

Define "soft-deleted" once and use it consistently. Either:

- **Option A (preferred):** treat a row as excluded/deleted whenever `status === 'deleted'` **or** `deletedBy` is non-empty, in `wl list` (and any other read path that projects "live" items). This makes visible rows always mutable.
- **Option B:** have the `wl update` soft-delete guard key on `status === 'deleted'` only, and treat `deletedBy` as pure attribution for non-deleted rows.

The chosen option must be applied to **every** read/selection path that can feed the release gate (`wl list --stage`, `wl worklist`, `wl next`), not just `wl list`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A single shared predicate function defines "soft-deleted" for both read and write paths.
- [ ] AC2: A row with non-empty `deletedBy` is either excluded from every list/selection path **or** is mutable via `wl update` — the two paths must agree (no visible-but-immutable rows).
- [ ] AC3: Regression test: an item with `status !== 'deleted'` but non-empty `deletedBy` has consistent treatment — if it is returned by `wl list --stage in_review`, `wl update` must accept a mutation on it; if it is excluded, `wl list` must not return it.
- [ ] AC4: Regression test: `wl list --stage in_review` never returns a row the release gate cannot audit (i.e. never a row for which `wl update --status in_progress` fails with `deleted-item`).
- [ ] AC5: `wl doctor` reports no findings introduced by the change; existing soft-deleted rows remain excluded from normal lists.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/list.ts` — `includeDeleted` filter (list-side predicate).
- `src/commands/update.ts` — soft-delete guard (`SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9`), `deleted-item` error.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — consolidated read path consumed by selection lists.
- `src/commands/next.ts` — dispatch selection path.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — sets `deletedBy` / `status=deleted`.
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — status/stage validation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MLB703EH1FNOQR1** — "Exlude deleted from list" (completed). Covers only `status === 'deleted'`; this item covers the `deletedBy` dimension it left out. Its fix commit added no tests.
- **WL-0MV2E2ZS5001RGLO** — `wl delete` lost-update / soft-delete convergence.
- **WL-0MTFNIRXU007X7U4** — delete-side protection: unattributed deletes never override live items.
- **MS-0MW22TQS8008021W** (separate project) — residual `wl doctor` findings; the ship-comment symptom that exposed this mismatch.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `deletedBy` is intended as the authoritative soft-delete marker (per `SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9`), so Option A is the safer reconciliation for read paths.
- **Risk — data semantics:** changing read-path visibility affects Herdr/TUI selection lists; the change must be rolled out with the shared predicate and its tests.
- **Risk — scope:** do not alter deletion attribution or merge/sync protection logic; only reconcile the predicate.
data.title: Inconsistent soft-delete predicate: wl list excludes only status=deleted while wl update rejects any non-empty deletedBy (visible-but-immutable rows block the release gate)

# Intake Brief: Fix `wl delete` deleteReason overwrite and add `--reason` flag

## Problem statement

`wl delete` unconditionally overwrites any existing `deleteReason` with the hardcoded string `"deleted via wl delete"` and offers no `--reason` flag. This destroys audit trails (operators who pre-set reasons lose them on delete) and defeats the delete-side merge protection introduced by WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO, because every CLI delete becomes "attributed" by a fabricated constant that cannot distinguish intent from absence of intent.

## Users

- **Bulk-cleanup operators**: agents or humans retiring stale backlog items who need each deletion to carry its specific rationale.
- **Merge-layer consumers**: the sync merge gate (`isAttributedDelete()`) that relies on `deleteReason` as a consent signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`wl delete` accepts `--reason <text>`** and stores it as `deleteReason`; the applied reason is echoed per id in `--json` output.
2. **When `--reason` is omitted, a pre-existing non-empty `deleteReason` is preserved.** The CLI must not pass a reason value that shadows the item's existing one — the `|| item.deleteReason` fallback in the database layer must become reachable.
3. **The default `"deleted via wl delete"` is applied only when no reason was supplied and the item has none already.** Crucially, this default must not, on its own, satisfy `isAttributedDelete()` from `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts:113`. The implementer decides: either the default is stored as empty (discarded for merge-gate purposes), or `isAttributedDelete()` is updated to exclude the CLI default string. Decision recorded in the implementation commit.
4. **Recursive deletion attributes each descendant distinctly** — at minimum the supplied (or preserved) reason plus the cascade source id — so a swept child is distinguishable from a deliberately retired item. Parent and descendants are reported separately in `--json` output.
5. **Tests cover:** (a) reason via `--reason` stored verbatim; (b) a pre-set reason survives delete with no `--reason`; (c) default applied only when item has none; (d) cascade records cascade source per descendant; (e) an unattributed CLI delete is **not** reported as an attributed delete (regression test for the merge gate).
6. **`wl update --delete-reason` on already-deleted items continues to work** as the documented repair path.

## Impact

Operators can record why an item was retired at the point of deletion, so bulk cleanups stay auditable and an accidental or intent-less delete can no longer masquerade as a deliberate one during a cross-agent sync merge.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing CLI consumers (JSON output contract, single-id legacy fields, batch semantics).
- Must not change the REST API's `deleted via API` default.
- The fix in `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` (the `|| item.deleteReason` fallback) must remain backward-compatible with API callers and any internal callers.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — hardcoded reason at line 82; add `--reason` option
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts:422-423` — `|| item.deleteReason` fallback (needs to become reachable)
- `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts:113` — `isAttributedDelete()` (may need updating per AC3 decision)
- `tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts` — test home for AC1-5
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` — ensure new flags don't affect auto-sync

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO** (completed) — Delete-side protection: the merge gate this defect defeats.
- **WL-0MVZ5Y0VR0065TPJ** (open, plan_complete) — Add `--deleted-by` and `--delete-reason` flags (CLI parity with REST API). Subsumed by this critical bug. Recommend closing once this item is scheduled.
- **WL-0MTFNIRXU007X7U4** (completed) — Delete-side protection implementation.
- **WL-0MU38HN2J008WWTB** (completed) — Repair path via `wl update --delete-reason`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The `--deleted-by` flag work from WL-0MVZ5Y0VR0065TPJ overlaps. If that item is not closed, it can become a child of this bug (or be folded into it). Decision: record as a decision in implementation.
- **Merge-gate regression:** Changing how `isAttributedDelete()` evaluates the default string could affect sync behaviour. A regression test must be written.
- **Backward compatibility:** Internal callers (API, other commands) may pass `deleteReason` explicitly. The fallback chain `opts?.deleteReason || item.deleteReason || ''` must handle `undefined`, `''`, and non-empty values correctly for all callers.
- **Assumption:** The `isAttributedDelete()` decision (AC3) should favour keeping the merge gate conservative — an unreasoned delete should not be treated as deliberate. The implementer should record the rationale in-code.

## Existing State

```
src/commands/delete.ts:82: const deleteReason = 'deleted via wl delete';
packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts:423: deleteReason: opts?.deleteReason || item.deleteReason || ''
```

Every `wl delete` invocation passes a non-empty literal, so the `|| item.deleteReason` fallback is never reached from the CLI. 216 of 847 deletions in the SA store carry the identical generic string, making them unauditable.

## Desired Change

- Add `--reason <text>` option to `wl delete`.
- When `--reason` is absent, do not pass a reason to the database layer so the existing `deleteReason` fallback kicks in.
- When both are absent, either store empty (merge-gate neutral) or a marker that `isAttributedDelete()` recognises as unattributed.
- Recursive deletes record cascade source per descendant.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required: the seed context supplied a complete problem definition, reproduction evidence, six testable acceptance criteria, impact analysis, key files and related work, so the intake proceeded on the existing content (idempotent — re-running intake reproduces this same result without duplicating entries).

- Q: (none) — seed context sufficed to draft a clear brief; no producer questions were asked.
- Accepted design preference recorded from the description (AC3): the `isAttributedDelete()` decision (discard the default in favour of an empty reason, **or** stop counting the CLI default as intent) is deferred to implementation time and must be recorded in the implementation commit. No producer input needed to draft the brief; the implementer records the rationale.
- OPEN DECISION (non-blocking, for the producer at scheduling): `WL-0MVZ5Y0VR0065TPJ` (`wl delete: add --deleted-by and --delete-reason flags`) is the medium-priority predecessor of this critical superset. It should be folded into this item (closed as subsumed) once this item is scheduled, so the merge-gate regression test is written once. Recorded here so the decision is not lost; does not block intake completion.
## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-08T18:40Z** — Plan decomposition: created 4 child tasks (TEST, CLI, DB, VERIFY) covering all 6 parent ACs in test-first dependency order. Effort: Extra Small. Risk: Low.
- **2026-11-08T18:40Z** — Automated review: all 6 stages passed. AC coverage: all 6 parent ACs covered.
- **2026-11-08T18:39Z** — Cleaned up 5 duplicate/autoclosed children (1 corrupted, 4 redundant).

Add --reason <text> option to the wl delete CLI command.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **wl delete accepts --reason <text>**: The CLI adds an --reason option that accepts a freeform text string. The option is positional: `wl delete <id> --reason "cleaning up stale items"`.
2. **Reason stored as deleteReason**: The provided reason is passed through the call chain to the database layer and stored as the item deleteReason.
3. **No reason supplied, no default passed**: When --reason is absent, the CLI must NOT pass any deleteReason value to the database layer. The existing fallback in the DB layer (`|| item.deleteReason`) becomes reachable, preserving any pre-set reason.
4. **Reason echoed in --json output**: When deleting with --reason, the applied reason appears in the JSON output per-id results.

- Add the --reason option in `src/commands/delete.ts` after the existing --no-recursive and --no-sync options.

- Pass the reason through to `db.delete(idLookup, recursive, { deletedBy, deleteReason })` — only when --reason was explicitly supplied, otherwise pass undefined so DB fallback reaches the item's existing deleteReason.

Verify the merge-gate decision (AC3), the repair path (AC6), and integration correctness.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC3 decision recorded in code**: The choice between (a) storing empty deleteReason when no --reason is supplied, and (b) updating isAttributedDelete() to exclude the CLI default string — is documented in an inline comment in the implementation. The chosen approach ensures the fabricated default does not, on its own, satisfy isAttributedDelete().
2. **AC5e regression test**: An unreasoned CLI delete (no --reason, no pre-existing deleteReason) does NOT satisfy isAttributedDelete(). Verify the predicate directly on the stored item after deletion.
3. **AC6 repair path verified**: wl update --delete-reason on an already-deleted item continues to set the field correctly. Add or update a test to prove the repair path still works after the fix.
4. **Integration with auto-sync**: The new --reason flag does not break auto-sync behavior — run delete-auto-sync.test.ts (existing test file) and verify it passes.
5. **Full delete test suite passes**: All delete-related tests pass (delete-batch.test.ts, delete-auto-sync.test.ts, delete-reason.test.ts).

## Merge-Gate Decision (AC3)

Recommended approach: **store empty when no reason**. Rationale:
- A fabricated constant is not attribution — it falsely signals intent that does not exist.
- The deletedBy field (configured user email) still provides "who" attribution.
- The merge gate's isAttributedDelete() checks `deletedBy || deleteReason`; with an empty deleteReason but a non-empty deletedBy, the item is still attributed by "who" alone — which is correct (the operator did delete it, they just didn't record why).
- If the intent is that an unreasoned delete must NOT be attributed at all, the CLI can also skip setting deletedBy — but that would break the existing contract (deletedBy is always set). The AC specifically targets deleteReason, not deletedBy.

Document this rationale in a code comment at the site where the default is removed from delete.ts.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — record the AC3 decision rationale

## Problem

The worklist header's host-budget counter (`[budget: implement n/max · audit n/max]`) counts the AUDIT tier with `reduceMarkerCounts` in `readHostBudgetStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts`): freshness only, no pane liveness. A ledger entry whose audit pane has CLOSED therefore still renders as `audit 1/1` until the 2 h heartbeat-staleness window expires. Observed 2026-11-08: item AH-0MW3MGY3Z003R1M6's audit completed at 20:21:59Z and its pane `w55:pWK` closed, yet the header still reported `audit 1/1` at 21:25Z with no audit pane open.

The sweep/release backstop (parent WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA) removes such entries, but only on a pane-close-reaper pass; with `paneCloseEnabled: false` it never runs, so the display has no independent correctness guarantee.

## Desired change

Make the audit DISPLAY count pane-aware in `readHostBudgetStatus`: a fresh confirmed entry whose `paneId` is absent from the trusted live pane list is excluded from the displayed audit count. Keep:

- unconfirmed entries (no `paneId`, reserve→spawn window) counted while fresh;
- confirmed entries with a live pane counted while fresh;
- stale entries excluded (unchanged);
- the legacy `active-audit` marker count (unchanged);
- the display strictly read-only (never reaps or rewrites the ledger).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `readHostBudgetStatus` does not count a fresh audit ledger entry whose non-empty `paneId` is absent from the supplied live pane list, so the header cannot claim a dead audit is live.
2. A fresh audit entry with no `paneId` (reserve→spawn window) is still counted; a fresh audit entry whose pane is live is still counted; stale entries remain excluded.
3. The display read remains strictly read-only: the ledger bytes are unchanged after the read.
4. Unit tests cover dead/live/unconfirmed/stale audit entries in the display count, and the existing implement-tier/legacy-marker behaviour is unchanged.
5. `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the pane-aware audit display rule and its deliberate divergence from the admission rule.
6. Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Out of scope

- Changing audit ADMISSION semantics (`readAuditBudgetState`/`freshCount`) or the 2 h staleness fallback.
- Enabling the pane-close reaper or decoupling the sweep (that is the parent item's / a sibling fix).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — new pure pane-aware audit display reduction.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — use it for the audit display count.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.test.ts` — display-count cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.test.ts` — pure reduction cases.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — document the rule.

## Impact

The worklist header stops reporting an audit in progress when the audit's pane is already gone, so the operator sees `audit 0/1` as soon as the audit pane closes instead of a phantom slot for up to two hours.

# Create shared isSoftDeleted predicate in @worklog/shared

## Goal

Define a single, exported `isSoftDeleted(item: WorkItem): boolean` predicate function in the shared package that determines whether a work item is soft-deleted.

## Definition

A work item is soft-deleted when:
- `status === 'deleted'` **OR**
- `deletedBy` is non-empty (truthy after trim)

This matches the current `wl update` soft-delete guard logic while also including the `status` dimension.

**Do not conflate with existing related-but-distinct predicates:**
- `isAttributedDelete` in `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` — delete *attribution* for merge protection, not visibility.
- `isDeleteIntent`/`Boolean(item.deletedBy) || Boolean(item.deleteReason)` in `src/claim-hold.ts` — claim-hold suppression.

Only the read/select/mutability predicate named in this epic is reconciled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC0 (parent AC1): A single shared predicate function defines "soft-deleted" for both read and write paths.
- [ ] AC1: `isSoftDeleted` is exported from `@worklog/shared` and importable by both `src/commands/list.ts` and `src/commands/update.ts`.
- [ ] AC2: `isSoftDeleted({ status: 'deleted', deletedBy: '' })` returns `true`.
- [ ] AC3: `isSoftDeleted({ status: 'completed', deletedBy: 'user@example.com' })` returns `true`.
- [ ] AC4: `isSoftDeleted({ status: 'completed', deletedBy: '' })` returns `false`.
- [ ] AC5: `isSoftDeleted({ status: 'open', deletedBy: '' })` returns `false`.
- [ ] AC6: Unit tests cover all four quadrants (deleted/alive x has/missing deletedBy).

## Key Files
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` - predicate definition beside the delete/attribution logic
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - re-export from the package entry point
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` - quadrant unit tests

## Dependencies
None - foundational utility.

## Problem

`tests/**` resolve `@worklog/shared` through the package `exports` map to the **built** output (`packages/shared/dist/`), which is gitignored. A checkout whose `packages/shared/dist` predates a change under `packages/shared/src` therefore exercises the OLD shared code, and the full suite reports failures for work that is already correct and merged.

Each implement worktree builds its own `packages/shared/dist`, so the dev-push gate (which tests the pushed commit in a clean/wt checkout) can be green while the long-lived main checkout stays stale — the failure then reappears in the main checkout, in audit runs and in any agent session that runs the suite from there.

## Evidence (2026-11-08)

- Main checkout `packages/shared/dist/database/work-items.js` was built 2026-11-07T13:46Z; commit `36d965a4` (WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7, 2026-11-08T21:22Z) changed `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` to add cascade delete attribution.
- A fresh full-suite run at dev HEAD `3dad96d4` (clean tree, `run_tests.py --type full --scope full --force`) failed 3 tests in `tests/cli/delete-reason.test.ts`: expected `cascade from <parent-id>: sweeping subtree`, received `sweeping subtree` (the pre-change behaviour).
- After `npm run build` in the same checkout the identical suite was green: 344 files / 4825 tests passed, 0 failed.

## Desired outcome

Make the mismatch visible instead of silent, e.g. any of:

- a guard that fails the suite (or `run_tests.py`) with an actionable message when `packages/shared/src` is newer than `packages/shared/dist`;
- a build step in the test runner for the workspace shared package (cost-aware, cache-keyed);
- a documented, enforced rebuild precondition for full-suite evidence in `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` / the test-skill reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-suite run in a checkout with a `packages/shared/dist` older than `packages/shared/src` either rebuilds it or fails immediately with an actionable message naming the rebuild command.
2. The guard/behaviour is covered by a test (stale and fresh dist cases).
3. `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (and the test-skill reference if behaviour lives in the runner) document the requirement.
4. The full project test suite passes.

## Impact

Agents and audits stop chasing phantom test failures caused by a stale local workspace build, so a red suite once again means the code is actually broken.

# Herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget

## Goal

Make the herdr downtime dispatcher's **audit-tier** capacity decision read the proxy's audit availability (the shared local resource) instead of asserting a per-host `budget.json` cap, so two ContextHub instances on different servers cannot independently believe they are under cap.

**discovered-from:** LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (llm worklog — "Serialise audits at the shared local resource, not per host or per repo").

**Producer direction (2026-11-09):** `budget.json` is managed per ContextHub host and ContextHub may run on several servers; it is better for the proxy to manage the budget and for ContextHub to query it than for each host to enforce its own cap.

## Problem

`getActiveAudit` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) reads the machine-scoped ledger (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`, `dispatch-budget.json`) and the per-host `budget.json` cap (`maxAudit`, default 1). The host-wide guard serialises audits **on one machine**, but the resource they contend for is the single local `llama-server` GPU shared by every host. Two ContextHub hosts enforcing one audit each produce two concurrent audits on one GPU — the 2026-11-03 incident. The `machine-coordination.ts` comment already records the limitation: "single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) is out of scope".

The proxy already owns the audit budget and the live audit-lease registry (sibling llm item LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK), and every ContextHub host already talks to the proxy for model traffic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Audit admission is proxy-derived.** For the audit tier only, `getActiveAudit` / the dispatch gate queries the proxy's audit-availability endpoint (cap, live leases, available) and does not assert the local `budget.json` cap. The implement tier keeps its existing per-host budget (out of scope).
- **AC2 — One vocabulary, no disagreement.** The refusal reason token and log vocabulary match the proxy's (`audit-budget-saturated`), so a dispatcher admission and a proxy refusal cannot disagree; a divergence is logged with both sides' evidence.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe on an unreachable proxy.** If the proxy cannot be reached, audit dispatch fails **closed** with a named reason (e.g. `audit-budget-unknown`) and logs the proxy error; the legacy local-ledger path remains behind an explicit flag for one release.
- **AC4 — Single-machine limitation documented.** The `~/.herdr/downtime` single-machine constraint and the chosen cross-machine mechanism (proxy-owned budget + query) are documented, superseding the "out of scope" note in `machine-coordination.ts`.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Tests cover: availability read maps to the dispatch decision; second audit refused with agreement between dispatcher and proxy; unreachable proxy fails closed; stale-lease reclamation reflected; the implement tier is unchanged. Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC6 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (gate table, machine-dir files, reason tokens, operator runbook), and `budget.json` is no longer documented as audit-authoritative.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Out of scope

- The proxy-side budget/lease implementation (sibling llm item LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK).
- Implement-tier budget changes.
- Multi-machine herdr leader election beyond audit admission.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` audit-tier query path.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — audit gate consumption of the proxy availability.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — legacy path behind a flag; availability vocabulary.
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — single-machine limitation note update.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` / `host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` — new acceptance tests.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** every ContextHub host can reach the proxy (it already proxies model traffic).
- **Risk:** a proxy outage now blocks audit dispatch (fail-closed). Mitigation: a named reason, operator-visible log, and the one-release legacy flag.
- **Scope-creep guard:** extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
